definition_zh: 风险管理；风险管控（识别、评估并降低损失可能性的系统做法）
definition_en: the systematic process of identifying, assessing and controlling the chance or impact of loss
core_image: 一张铺开的表格把每个可能出事的环节标成不同颜色，旁边一栏写着由谁去处理
scene: 暴雨将至，工地的安全主管把高空作业的吊篮全部收回，让班组改做室内检查。Before the storm, the site's risk management team lowered every suspended platform and moved the crews indoors.
sceneCN: 这里指「把可能出事的环节先找出来并安排应对的整套做法」（第 1 个义项：系统地识别、评估并控制损失可能）；句意为暴雨前，工地的风险管理小组把所有悬吊平台降下，并把班组转到室内作业。可辨识物件：安全帽、气象雷达屏、吊篮、检查清单。

pos.zh: 风险管理（不可数，指一整套做法）
作定语：风险管理的（如风险管理框架）

forms.label: 动词短语（实施风险管理）

derivatives.zh: 由基础名词加表示执行者的复合成分 → 执行风险管理的人
短语的基础名词，本义「危险」→ 风险
基础名词加形容词后缀，义为「充满……」→ 有风险的
基础动词，借自意大利语「操控、驯马」→ 操控；管理
基础动词加名词后缀，义为「行为或群体」→ 管理；管理层
由「管理者」加形容词后缀，义为「属于……」→ 管理上的

senses.title: The systematic process of handling risk
senses.titleCN: 系统处理风险的全过程
senses.definition: the organized process of finding, measuring and reducing threats before they turn into losses
senses.definitionCN: 在威胁变成损失之前，有组织地发现、衡量并减少它的过程
senses.example: The plant's risk management begins with a walk-through of every production line.
senses.exampleCN: 该厂的风险管理从走遍每一条生产线开始。
senses.why: risk names the uncertain harm and management names the controlled handling, so the phrase is literally the handling of uncertain harm.
senses.whyCN: 风险指不确定的损害，管理指有控制的处理，连起来就是「对不确定损害的处理」。

senses.title: The department that runs it
senses.titleCN: 承担这项工作的部门
senses.definition: the unit or team inside an organization that is responsible for the process
senses.definitionCN: 组织内部负责执行这一过程的部门或小组
senses.example: Risk management signed off on the new supplier after a credit check.
senses.exampleCN: 风险管理部门在信用审查后批准了这家新供应商。
senses.why: because the work is permanent, the phrase metonymically names the people and the office that carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 因为这项工作长期存在，整个短语便以转喻指执行它的人和部门。

senses.title: Market, credit and liquidity risk in finance
senses.titleCN: 金融领域的市场、信用与流动性风险
senses.definition: the practice of measuring and limiting the financial exposures of a bank or fund
senses.definitionCN: 衡量并限制银行或基金所承担金融敞口的做法
senses.example: Traders must keep their positions inside the limits set by risk management.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员必须把持仓保持在风险管理部门设定的限额之内。
senses.why: finance split the general idea into named exposures, so the phrase became a technical label for limits on money at risk.
senses.whyCN: 金融业把笼统的概念拆成有名目的敞口，这个短语于是成了「限定资金风险」的技术标签。

senses.title: Company-wide, or enterprise, risk
senses.titleCN: 覆盖整个企业的风险管理
senses.definition: a firm-wide view that compares and balances risks across all departments at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时比较并平衡各部门风险的全公司视角
senses.example: Enterprise risk management treats a supplier failure and a currency swing as one portfolio of threats.
senses.exampleCN: 企业风险管理把供应商断供与汇率波动当作同一组威胁来处理。
senses.why: once each department had its own risks, firms needed a level above them all, which is why enterprise was added to the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 各部门都有各自的风险之后，企业需要一个高于它们的层面，于是短语前加上了「企业」这一限定。

senses.title: Risk control on a project
senses.titleCN: 具体项目上的风险控制
senses.definition: the discipline of listing, ranking and answering threats to a project's cost, time and quality
senses.definitionCN: 列出、排序并回应项目成本、工期与质量所受威胁的做法
senses.example: The tunnel project keeps a risk register that is reviewed every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 这个隧道项目保留一份每周五复核的风险登记表。
senses.why: projects are temporary and each has its own deadline, so the same process is applied on a short horizon and called project risk management.
senses.whyCN: 项目是临时的，各有截止期限，同一套流程被放到短周期上使用，就称为项目风险管理。

senses.title: Transferring risk to an insurer
senses.titleCN: 通过保险转移风险
senses.definition: the use of insurance and contracts to move a loss to another party for a price
senses.definitionCN: 用保险与合同把损失以一定价格转移给另一方的做法
senses.example: Buying cover is risk management by transfer rather than by prevention.
senses.exampleCN: 购买保险属于以转移而非预防来进行的风险管理。
senses.why: the phrase covers not only reducing a threat but also deciding who should carry it, and insurance is the oldest such tool.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语不只包含减少威胁，也包含决定由谁承担，保险就是最古老的此类工具。

senses.title: Cyber and information risk
senses.titleCN: 网络与信息风险的管理
senses.definition: the protection of data and systems through access rules, backups and response drills
senses.definitionCN: 通过访问规则、备份与演练保护数据与系统的做法
senses.example: The hospital's risk management now includes phishing drills for every ward clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院的风险管理如今包括让每个病区文员参加钓鱼邮件演练。
senses.why: digital systems created a new class of loss that is cheap to prevent and expensive to suffer, so the same label was extended to them.
senses.whyCN: 数字系统带来了一类新的损失：预防便宜、承受昂贵，同一标签于是延伸到这一领域。

senses.title: Managing personal health risk
senses.titleCN: 个人健康风险的管理
senses.definition: the everyday use of the same logic on one's own body, money and habits
senses.definitionCN: 把同样的逻辑用在自身身体、金钱与习惯上的日常说法
senses.example: Her doctor called her diet and exercise plan a form of risk management.
senses.exampleCN: 她的医生把她那份饮食与运动计划称作一种风险管理。
senses.why: the phrase moved from offices into clinics and homes because individuals also weigh a small present cost against a large future loss.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语从办公室走进诊所与家庭，因为个人同样会用眼前的小成本换取未来的大损失。

senses.title: Disaster and climate risk reduction
senses.titleCN: 灾害与气候风险的降低
senses.definition: public planning that lowers the damage expected from floods, heat and other natural shocks
senses.definitionCN: 为降低洪水、高温等自然冲击所造成损害而做的公共规划
senses.example: Coastal cities now treat flood risk management as a budget priority.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海城市如今把洪水风险管理列为预算优先项。
senses.why: public bodies borrowed the corporate term for the same arithmetic of likelihood and damage, applied to whole populations.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构借用了企业术语，因为其背后是同一套「可能性乘以损害」的算法，只是对象换成全体居民。

intro.en: The phrase joins risk, a word of uncertain Italian origin that reached English through French, with management, which descends from Latin manus 'hand' by way of an Italian verb for handling horses. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由 risk 与 management 合成：前者源自意大利语、来源不确定，经法语进入英语；后者经意大利语中「驯马、操控」的动词上溯到拉丁语 manus「手」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Risk first appears in Italian trading records as risco or rischio, meaning a hazard run in shipping. Its deeper origin is uncertain: a link to a Latin verb for cutting away, and a link to a Greek word for root or cliff, are both hypotheses, and neither is settled.
items.cn: 风险一词最早见于意大利商业记录，写作 risco 或 rischio，指航运中要冒的危险。其更深来源不确定：把它连到拉丁语「切去」的动词，或连到希腊语「根、崖」的词，都只是假说，均无定论。

items.en: French took the Italian word as risque, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century. The early English sense was the chance of loss in trade or at sea, not yet a formal discipline.
items.cn: 法语把这个意大利词吸收为 risque，英语于 16 世纪借用。早期英语义为贸易或海上的损失可能，还不是一门正式学问。

items.en: By the seventeenth century risk was used for any uncertain harm that could be priced, insured or shared, which prepared the ground for the later compound.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，风险已用于任何可以被定价、投保或分担的不确定损害，为此后的复合词铺路。

items.en: Manage came from Italian maneggiare 'to handle, to train a horse', built on mano 'hand', from Latin manus. The horse sense gives the word its feel of skilled, repeated control.
items.cn: 管理一词来自意大利语 maneggiare「操控、驯马」，基于 mano「手」，再上溯拉丁语 manus。驯马的义感让这个词带上「熟练而反复的控制」意味。

items.en: The noun management first named the act of handling something, then the group of people who conduct an enterprise, a shift recorded in business writing of the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 名词管理先指操控某物的动作，后指经营企业的一群人，这一转变见于 19 世纪的商业写作。

items.en: The full phrase took hold in the mid-twentieth century, when engineering, insurance and finance began to treat the control of risk as a measurable professional routine.
items.cn: 整个短语在 20 世纪中叶站住脚，当时工程、保险与金融开始把风险控制当作可计量的职业常规。

note.en: The first group holds look-alike words built on risk or on the handling root; the second holds near neighbours that name narrower or adjacent practices.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「风险」或「操控」词干、形近的词；第二组是范围更窄或相邻的近似说法。

entries.definition: Carrying danger; it describes the exposure itself, while risk management describes what is done about it.
entries.definitionCN: 指带有危险；它描述敞口本身，而风险管理描述针对敞口做了什么。

entries.definition: Claimed to carry no danger; the phrase is a goal, not the process that pursues it.
entries.definitionCN: 声称没有危险；这是一个目标，而不是追求它的过程。

entries.definition: To handle or control something with skill; management is its noun, and the compound adds what is being handled.
entries.definitionCN: 指以技巧操控；管理是其名词形式，复合词则补出所操控的对象。

entries.definition: To handle something badly; the prefix marks failure, the reverse of what the discipline aims at.
entries.definitionCN: 指处理得很糟；前缀标记失败，与该学问的目标相反。

entries.definition: The act of making a loss smaller; it is one stage inside risk management, not the whole cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 指使损失变小；它只是风险管理内部的一个环节，不是整个循环。

entries.definition: A contract that pays for a loss after it happens; it transfers risk rather than removing its cause.
entries.definitionCN: 指损失发生后予以赔付的合同；它转移风险，而非消除成因。

entries.definition: Work that prevents injury to people, usually in one workplace; risk management also weighs money and reputation.
entries.definitionCN: 指防止人身伤害的工作，通常限于一个场所；风险管理还要权衡金钱与声誉。

entries.definition: Taking an offsetting position so that a price move hurts less; it is one technique within the wider process.
entries.definitionCN: 指建立对冲头寸以减轻价格波动伤害；它是整个流程中的一种技术。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Risk is the uncertain harm; management is the skilled handling: the phrase reads as handling harm before it lands.
normal.cn: 风险是不确定的损害，管理是熟练的处理：整个短语读作「在损害落地前处理它」。

normal.en: The word family runs risk, risky, risk-free, risk manager, manage, management, managerial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括风险、有风险的、无风险的、风险经理、管理、管理层、管理上的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the level: enterprise, financial, project and operational risk management.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出层级：企业、金融、项目与运营风险管理。

normal.en: Manage came from horse training, so the image is a rider keeping an animal on course, not a clerk filing papers.
normal.cn: 管理一词来自驯马，所以意象是骑手让牲畜走在正路上，而不是文员整理文件。

normal.en: Insurance is the oldest branch: pay a small certain sum to avoid a large uncertain one.
normal.cn: 保险是最古老的分支：付出一笔确定的小钱，躲开一笔不确定的大钱。

abstract.en: Picture a weather map where every red patch already has a name beside it and a person assigned to it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张气象图，每块红色区域旁边都已写好名字，并指定了负责人。

abstract.en: Picture a ship's captain who sails anyway, but only after counting the lifeboats.
abstract.cn: 想象一位船长照旧出海，只是在数清救生艇之后才起锚。

abstract.en: Picture a household that keeps one drawer of candles and water, and never needs to think about it again.
abstract.cn: 想象一户人家在抽屉里备好蜡烛与清水，此后就不必再为此担心。

examples.en: Good risk management does not remove uncertainty; it makes the cost of being wrong bearable.
examples.cn: 好的风险管理并不消除不确定性，而是让判断出错的代价变得可以承受。

examples.en: The bank's risk management blocked the trade because it exceeded the single-name limit.
examples.cn: 银行的风险管理部门否决了这笔交易，因为它超过了单一对手方的限额。

examples.en: Flood risk management saved the district more than the new drainage system cost.
examples.cn: 洪水风险管理为该区挽回的损失超过了新排水系统的造价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「风险」加「管理」——先把可能出事的环节找出来，再安排人去管住它 → 风险管理

root: risk 源自意大利语 risco／rischio「航运中的危险」，经法语 risque 进入英语，更深来源不确定（有「切去」与「根、崖」两种假说）；management 经意大利语 maneggiare「操控、驯马」上溯拉丁语 manus「手」，加名词后缀而成。整个短语在 20 世纪中叶成为专业术语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one cycle: find the exposure, measure it, decide who carries it, and keep watching it. The cycle is then applied to money, to a whole firm, to a project, to an insurer, to a network, to a body and to a city.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个循环展开：先找出敞口，再衡量它，决定由谁承担，然后持续观察。这个循环再被用到金钱、整个企业、单个项目、保险公司、网络、个人身体与一座城市上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chart of every weak point, each with a colour, a name and a countermeasure beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张列满薄弱环节的图表，每一处都配有颜色、负责人与应对办法。

branches.en: PROCESS AND OFFICE: the same cycle is both a method and the team that runs it.
branches.cn: 流程与部门：同一个循环既是一套方法，也是执行它的团队。

branches.en: MONEY AND THE WHOLE FIRM: exposures are priced in markets, then balanced across every department at once.
branches.cn: 金钱与整个企业：敞口先在市场中被定价，再在各部门之间整体平衡。

branches.en: SHORT HORIZON AND TRANSFER: a project runs the cycle to a deadline, and insurance moves the loss to another party.
branches.cn: 短周期与转移：项目把循环跑到截止日，保险则把损失移给另一方。

branches.en: DIGITAL SURFACE: data and networks add a cheap-to-prevent, costly-to-suffer class of loss.
branches.cn: 数字表面：数据与网络添上一类「预防便宜、承受昂贵」的损失。

branches.en: BODY AND CITY: the same arithmetic is used on one person's habits and on a whole coastline.
branches.cn: 身体与城市：同一套算法被用在个人习惯上，也被用在整条海岸线上。

intro.en: The phrase is a native compound of two borrowed words. The risk half is of uncertain Romance origin; the manage half carries a Latin root for hand plus an Italian verb for handling.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个借词构成的原生复合词。前半「风险」的罗曼语来源不确定；后半「管理」带拉丁语「手」的词根与意大利语「操控」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Only the manage half has a clear Latin ancestor: manus 'hand' anchors the family that runs manage, manager, managerial and management.
latinIntro.cn: 只有「管理」这一半有清楚的拉丁语祖先：manus「手」支撑起管理、经理、管理上的与管理层这一族词。

items.example: The lender priced the risk into the interest rate.
items.exampleCN: 放贷方把这一风险计入利率。

items.example: The shortcut is risky in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这条捷径在冬天很危险。
没有投资是真正无风险的。

items.meaning: the person who runs the process
items.example: The risk manager chairs the weekly review.
items.exampleCN: 风险经理主持每周复核。

items.example: The manager approved the new schedule.

items.meaning: the act or body of managing
items.exampleCN: 管理层削减了差旅预算。

items.example: The workload is manageable this month.
items.exampleCN: 这个月的工作量还应付得来。

items.example: The fund was mismanaged for years.
items.exampleCN: 这只基金多年来管理失当。

definition_zh: 推测；猜测；投机（尤指在金融市场上押注价格变化）
definition_en: the forming of a judgment without firm evidence, or the buying and selling of assets in the hope of gain from price changes
core_image: 一个人站在高塔上举着望远镜看远方，塔下同时摆着一张押注单和一本笔记
scene: 央行声明发布前，老交易员盯着行情屏加仓，赌利率会往下走。The old trader added to his position before the statement, pure speculation on falling rates.
sceneCN: 这里指「在信息不足时押注价格走向的金融投机」（第 2 个义项：买进或卖出资产，赌未来价格变化带来收益）；句意为声明发布之前，这位老交易员加仓，纯粹是在赌利率下行。可辨识物件：行情屏、望远镜、押注单、笔记本。

pos.zh: 推测；猜测；投机（可数或不可数，复数 speculations）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁分词词干加动词后缀 → 推测；投机
由该动词加形容词后缀，义为「倾向于……」→ 推测的；投机性的
由该动词加施事后缀 → 投机者；推测者
由形容词加副词后缀 → 凭推测地；投机地
由形容词加名词后缀，表性质 → 推测性；投机性

senses.title: A theory built without firm evidence
senses.titleCN: 在证据不足时形成的推断
senses.definition: a judgment or opinion formed about something that is not yet known for certain
senses.definitionCN: 对尚未确定之事形成的判断或看法
senses.example: Her speculation that the meeting would be postponed proved correct.
senses.exampleCN: 她关于会议将推迟的推测后来被证明是对的。
senses.why: the word names the act of looking out from a height, so the core is seeing what is not yet in front of you, then guessing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指从高处向外瞭望，核心是先看见尚未到眼前的事，再去猜。

senses.title: Betting on price movements in markets
senses.titleCN: 在金融市场上押注价格变化
senses.definition: the practice of buying or selling an asset in the hope of a profit from a price change rather than from its use
senses.definitionCN: 买进或卖出资产，指望从价格变化而非使用中获得利润的做法
senses.example: Heavy speculation in copper drove the price far above its production cost.
senses.exampleCN: 对铜的大量投机把价格推到远高于生产成本的水平。
senses.why: finance kept the looking-ahead image but made the guess a position: money is placed on a future price.
senses.whyCN: 金融保留了「向前看」的意象，却把猜测变成头寸：把钱押在一个未来价格上。

senses.title: A single offered guess
senses.titleCN: 一次具体的猜测或说法
senses.definition: one countable guess or opinion that a person puts forward
senses.definitionCN: 某个人提出的一个可数猜测或看法
senses.example: The report's central speculation is that the tomb was robbed in antiquity.
senses.exampleCN: 该报告的核心猜测是这座墓在古代就被盗过。
senses.why: because one guess is a countable thing, the noun takes a plural and can be introduced by a or the.
senses.whyCN: 因为一个猜测是可数之物，这个名词有复数形式，也能用不定冠词或定冠词引出。

senses.title: Talk about other people's private affairs
senses.titleCN: 对他人私事的议论与猜测
senses.definition: idle or intrusive guessing about someone's private life, often treated as a mild vice
senses.definitionCN: 对他人私生活作出的闲散或侵入式猜测，常被视为轻度的不良习惯
senses.example: The tabloids fed speculation about the couple's separation.
senses.exampleCN: 小报助长了关于这对夫妇分居的猜测。
senses.why: the same word covers guessing that has no financial stake at all, which is why it also names gossip.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也涵盖完全无关金钱的猜测，因此也指闲话。

senses.title: Pure reasoning about what cannot be observed
senses.titleCN: 对无法观察之物进行的纯粹思辨
senses.definition: reasoning that follows a question beyond the reach of observation, as in philosophy and theology
senses.definitionCN: 把问题推到观察所不能及之处进行推理，如哲学与神学中的思辨
senses.example: Medieval speculation on the nature of light drew on both optics and scripture.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪关于光的本质的思辨同时借助光学与经文。
senses.why: the sense is old and respectable: when the object cannot be seen, looking out from the tower becomes careful thought.
senses.whyCN: 这一义既古老又体面：当对象看不见时，从塔上向外看就变成了审慎的思考。

senses.title: Buying property to profit from its price
senses.titleCN: 为从房价上涨中获利而买房
senses.definition: the purchase of land or buildings mainly to resell at a higher price
senses.definitionCN: 主要为以更高价转手而购买土地或房屋
senses.example: Speculation in land on the city's edge pushed prices beyond local wages.
senses.exampleCN: 对城市边缘土地的投机把价格推高到超过当地工资的水平。
senses.why: property is the classic case where use value is small and expected gain is large, so the financial sense attaches easily.
senses.whyCN: 房产是使用价值小、预期收益大的典型情形，金融义便自然附着上来。

senses.title: Holding an asset for gain, not for use
senses.titleCN: 持有资产为了获利而非使用
senses.definition: in economics, the demand for an asset or for cash because a price is expected to rise
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中因预期价格上升而产生对资产或现金的需求
senses.example: Keynes described the speculative motive for holding cash when bond yields are expected to rise.
senses.exampleCN: 凯恩斯描述过在预期债券收益率上升时持有现金的投机动机。
senses.why: economics separated the holding motive from the trading act, so the word now also labels a reason for keeping an asset idle.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把持有动机与交易动作分开，这个词于是也标注「让资产闲置」的一种理由。

senses.title: The old sense of watching from a height
senses.titleCN: 古代「从高处观察」的本义
senses.definition: the historical sense of observing or spying from a lookout point, now archaic
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指从瞭望点观察或窥探，今已古旧
senses.example: The Latin noun first meant a lookout, and only later a guess.
senses.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词最初指瞭望处，后来才指猜测。
senses.why: keeping this older layer explains the spelling: the tower is still visible inside the modern word.
senses.whyCN: 保留这一更早的层次能解释拼写：现代词里仍看得见那座塔。

intro.en: Speculation comes from Latin speculatio 'a lookout, a watching', from speculari 'to watch, to spy', built on specula 'watchtower', itself from specere 'to look'. The financial sense is a later narrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: speculation 来自拉丁 speculatio「瞭望、观察」，出自动词 speculari「观察、窥探」，其词干 specula 意为「瞭望塔」，再上溯 specere「看」。金融义是后来收窄的结果。年代均为约数。

items.en: Specere meant 'to look, to observe'. Its older Indo-European history is reconstructed rather than directly attested, and the same stock also gives words for inspecting and for spectacle.
items.cn: specere 意为「看、观察」。它更早的印欧语历史属于重构而非直接有证，同一词干还给出「检查」与「景象」等词。

items.en: A specula was a watchtower or lookout, the raised place from which a guard could see approaching danger.
items.cn: specula 指瞭望塔或观察哨，即守卫能看见危险逼近的高处。

items.en: The verb speculari meant 'to watch from a height, to spy, to examine', and it kept the sense of purposeful looking rather than mere seeing.
items.cn: 动词 speculari 意为「从高处观察、窥探、审视」，保留的是有目的的看，而非单纯的看见。

items.en: The noun speculatio named both the act of watching and, by extension, the conclusions a watcher might form about what was coming.
items.cn: 名词 speculatio 既指观察的动作，也引申指观察者对将发生之事可能形成的结论。

items.en: English took the noun in the fourteenth century as speculation. Early uses covered observation, inquiry and conjecture on matters hard to see.
items.cn: 英语于 14 世纪以 speculation 吸收该名词。早期用法涵盖观察、探究与对难以看见之事的猜想。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word was applied to ventures whose return depended on a future price, and by the nineteenth century this was the dominant commercial sense.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，这个词被用于收益取决于未来价格的事业；到 19 世纪，这已成为主要的商业义。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same looking root or close in shape; the second holds words for guessing and for betting, each with a different weight.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「看」这个词根或形近的词；第二组是猜测与押注类近义词，分量各不相同。

entries.definition: To form a guess or to take a market position; the noun names either the guess or the position.
entries.definitionCN: 指作出猜测或建立市场头寸；名词则指猜测或头寸本身。

entries.definition: Based on guesswork or carrying financial risk; it describes the quality, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指基于猜测或带有金融风险；它描述性质，而非动作。

entries.definition: One who takes such positions; the noun speculation names what that person does.
entries.definitionCN: 指建立此类头寸的人；名词投机则指此人所做的事。

entries.definition: Specere 'to look' plus a suffix gave a public show; the sense is passive seeing, not guessing.
entries.definitionCN: 「看」的词根加后缀给出「公开景象」；其义为被动地看见，而非猜测。

entries.definition: To look closely into something for a purpose; it lacks the forward, uncertain reach of speculation.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某目的仔细查看；它缺少投机那种朝前、不确定的延伸。

entries.definition: A conclusion offered on incomplete grounds; it stresses the weakness of the evidence more than speculation does.
entries.definitionCN: 指在证据不完整时提出的结论；它比投机更强调证据薄弱。

entries.definition: A stated proposition put up for testing; it is meant to be checked, while speculation may never be.
entries.definitionCN: 指为检验而提出的明确命题；它本就打算被验证，而猜测未必。

entries.definition: Staking money on a random outcome; speculation at least claims a reading of the market.
entries.definitionCN: 指把钱押在随机结果上；投机至少声称读过市场。

entries.definition: Money put into an asset for income or long-term growth; the line between it and speculation is drawn by intent and risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指为收益或长期增长投入资产的钱；它与投机的界线由意图与风险划定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The tower is still inside the word: a watcher on a high platform guesses what is coming.
normal.cn: 那座塔仍在词里：高台上的观察者猜测将要发生什么。

normal.en: The family runs speculate, speculation, speculative, speculator, speculatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括推测、猜测、推测性的、投机者、凭推测地。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate the kinds: pure speculation, market speculation, speculation in property.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把类型分开：纯属猜测、市场投机、房地产投机。

normal.en: The same looking root appears in inspect and spectacle, both about seeing rather than betting.
normal.cn: 同一个「看」的词根出现在检查与景象二词中，二者都关乎看见而非押注。

normal.en: Finance marks the difference by intent: use the asset and it is investment; wait for its price and it is speculation.
normal.cn: 金融业以意图划界：使用资产叫投资，等它的价格叫投机。

abstract.en: Picture a guard in a tower before dawn, guessing which road the carts will take.
abstract.cn: 想象天没亮时塔上的守卫，猜运货的车会走哪条路。

abstract.en: Picture a coin held above a table, neither side yet showing.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币悬在桌面上方，哪一面都还没露出。

abstract.en: Picture a row of house shells with no families in them, bought only for the price tag.
abstract.cn: 想象一排没有住户的空壳房，买下它们只为那张价签。

examples.en: Speculation about the cause of the fire filled the newspapers for a week.
examples.cn: 关于起火原因的猜测在报纸上持续了一周。

examples.en: The tax was meant to curb speculation in empty apartments.
examples.cn: 这项税意在遏制对空置公寓的投机。

examples.en: Without data, any explanation of the collapse remains speculation.
examples.cn: 没有数据，对这次崩塌的任何解释都只是猜测。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看」的词根加名词后缀——站在塔上往远处看，看不清就只好猜；把钱押在猜的结果上就是投机

root: 拉丁 speculatio「瞭望、观察」来自 speculari（specula「瞭望塔」+ specere「看」）；同根词有 inspect、spectacle、perspective；金融义为 18 至 19 世纪的收窄。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one posture: a watcher on a height looks at what has not arrived. The looking becomes a guess, the guess becomes talk, then thought, then a position in a market, then a reason to hold an asset.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一个姿态出发：观察者站在高处，看向尚未到来的事。看变成猜测，猜测变成议论，再变成思辨，再变成市场上的头寸，最后变成持有资产的理由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watcher on a tower looks toward a future he cannot yet see clearly.
core.cn: 核心意象：塔上的观察者朝一个还看不清楚的未来望去。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL POSTURE: watching from a height is the oldest layer and still explains the spelling.
branches.cn: 最初的姿态：从高处观察是最古老的一层，至今仍能解释拼写。

branches.en: GUESS MADE PUBLIC: one guess is countable, and many guesses become talk about other people.
branches.cn: 被说出的猜测：一个猜测可数，许多猜测就成了对他人的议论。

branches.en: THOUGHT WITHOUT OBSERVATION: when the object cannot be seen, looking turns into reasoning.
branches.cn: 不靠观察的思考：对象看不见时，看就转为推理。

branches.en: MONEY ON A PRICE: the guess is converted into a position, in any market including land.
branches.cn: 押在价格上的钱：猜测被换成头寸，可用于任何市场，包括土地。

branches.en: A MOTIVE TO HOLD: economics names the reason for keeping cash or an asset idle.
branches.cn: 持有的动机：经济学为让现金或资产闲置给出理由。

intro.en: Speculation is a Latin noun of root plus suffix; the root means 'to look', and a tower stands between the looking and the guessing.
intro.cn: 「猜测」是词根加后缀的拉丁名词；词根意为「看」，一座塔立在「看」与「猜」之间。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere 'to look' yields specula, speculari and speculatio, and the same root reaches English in inspect, spectacle and perspective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 specere「看」衍生出瞭望塔、观察与猜测，同一词根还以检查、景象与透视进入英语。

items.example: The root supplies the act of looking.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「看」的动作。

items.example: The guard watched the road from the tower.
The verb adds purpose to plain seeing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给单纯的看见加上目的。

items.example: The word entered English in the fourteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个词于 14 世纪进入英语。

items.meaning: to conjecture; to trade on price
items.example: Analysts speculate about the next move.
items.exampleCN: 分析师推测下一步动作。
这些收益纯属投机所得。

items.meaning: one who conjectures or trades on price
items.example: The speculator bought the whole block.
items.exampleCN: 这名投机者买下了整片街区。

items.example: The parade was a fine spectacle.
items.exampleCN: 这场游行是极好的景象。

items.meaning: a way of seeing through to depth
items.example: The hill gives a perspective on the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这座小山提供了俯瞰山谷的视角。

latinEntries.structure: speculari, speculatus sum (deponent verb, first conjugation)

definition_zh: 推测的；猜测性的；投机性的（金融上指高风险、指望价差获利）
definition_en: based on guesswork rather than firm evidence, or carrying a high financial risk in the hope of a large gain
core_image: 一张尚未完工的蓝图压在几枚硬币下面，图纸边角还写着几个问号
scene: 分析师在报告里用「可能」和「如果」连着写了三页，最后承认这些结论都只是推测性的。The analyst filled three pages with maybes and ifs, then admitted that the conclusions were speculative.
sceneCN: 这里指「建立在猜测而非确证之上的」（第 1 个义项：结论依赖未经验证的假设）；句意为分析师写了三页「可能」与「如果」，最后承认这些结论都只是推测性的。可辨识物件：未完工的蓝图、硬币、问号、批注笔。

pos.zh: 推测的；猜测性的；投机性的

由同一拉丁词干逆构出的动词 → 推测；投机

senses.title: Resting on guesswork
senses.titleCN: 建立在猜测之上
senses.definition: formed from conjecture rather than from proof or direct observation
senses.definitionCN: 由猜测而非证明或直接观察形成
senses.example: The dating of the layer remains speculative until the pottery is analysed.
senses.exampleCN: 在陶器完成分析之前，这一地层的年代仍是推测性的。
senses.why: the adjective adds a quality to the act of guessing, so it describes any claim whose support is not yet there.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词给「猜测」这一动作加上性质，因此描述任何尚缺支撑的主张。

senses.title: Financially risky in pursuit of gain
senses.titleCN: 为求收益而承担高金融风险
senses.definition: describing an investment whose return depends on an expected price change and may easily be lost
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种收益取决于预期价差、且很可能全部损失的投资
senses.example: Regulators warned that the new fund was too speculative for small savers.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构警告说，这只新基金对小型储户来说投机性太强。
senses.why: in finance the quality is attached to the position rather than the theory: the guess is now backed by money.
senses.whyCN: 在金融中，这一性质附着于头寸而非理论：猜测此时已由金钱背书。

senses.title: Purely theoretical inquiry
senses.titleCN: 纯理论性的探究
senses.definition: concerned with reasoning about matters that cannot be settled by experiment
senses.definitionCN: 关心无法用实验定论的问题的推理
senses.example: Medieval scholars divided speculative philosophy from practical ethics.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪学者把思辨哲学与实践伦理分开。
senses.why: the old academic sense treats speculation as an honourable activity, so the adjective marks thought that seeks truth rather than use.
senses.whyCN: 古老的学术义把思辨视为体面活动，因此这个形容词标记「求真理而非求实用」的思考。

senses.title: A mind inclined to guess
senses.titleCN: 倾向于猜测的性格
senses.definition: describing a person whose habit is to form conclusions quickly on limited grounds
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个人习惯凭有限依据迅速下结论
senses.example: He has a speculative turn of mind and trusts his hunches too soon.
senses.exampleCN: 他天性爱推测，对自己的直觉信得太快。
senses.why: the adjective can describe the person as well as the claim, which is why it also names a temperament.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既能描述主张，也能描述人，因此也指一种性情。

senses.title: Speculative fiction as a genre
senses.titleCN: 作为文类的推想小说
senses.definition: naming stories that invent worlds beyond the present one, such as science fiction and fantasy
senses.definitionCN: 指发明超越当下世界的叙事，如科幻与奇幻
senses.example: The course reads speculative fiction alongside the history of technology.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课把推想小说与技术史放在一起读。
senses.why: the genre label extends the idea of imagining what is not yet here from markets to whole invented worlds.
senses.whyCN: 这一文类标签把「想象尚未存在之物」从市场扩展到整个虚构世界。

senses.title: An unsolicited speculative approach
senses.titleCN: 未经邀约的试探性申请
senses.definition: describing a job application or business inquiry sent without an advertised opening
senses.definitionCN: 描述在没有公开招聘时主动寄出的求职申请或商业询问
senses.example: She sent a speculative application to the publisher and got a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 她向这家出版社寄了一份试探性申请，并收到了回复。
senses.why: because nothing has been offered yet, the approach itself is a guess that a place might exist.
senses.whyCN: 因为对方尚未提供职位，这种主动接触本身就是「也许有空缺」的猜测。

senses.title: Describing an inflated asset price
senses.titleCN: 描述被吹高的资产价格
senses.definition: describing prices that have risen because buyers expect further rises rather than because of earnings
senses.definitionCN: 描述因买者预期继续上涨、而非因盈利上升而抬高的价格
senses.example: The land market turned speculative long before construction began.
senses.exampleCN: 早在地基动工之前，土地市场就已变得投机化。
senses.why: when a whole market takes on the quality, the adjective shifts from one trade to the level of prices.
senses.whyCN: 当整个市场带上这种性质，形容词就从单笔交易转到价格水平。

senses.title: The speculative motive in economics
senses.titleCN: 经济学中的投机动机
senses.definition: naming the reason to hold cash or an asset because its price is expected to change favourably
senses.definitionCN: 指因预期价格将有利变化而持有现金或资产的理由
senses.example: Keynes treated the speculative motive as one of three reasons for holding money.
senses.exampleCN: 凯恩斯把投机动机视为持有货币的三种理由之一。
senses.why: economics turned the adjective into a named category of behaviour, which is its most technical use.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把这个形容词变成一个有名字的行为类别，这是其最技术的用法。

intro.en: Speculative is the Latin-derived adjective of speculation: speculativus came from speculari 'to watch', and English took it through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: speculative 是 speculation 的拉丁系形容词：speculativus 出自 speculari「观察」，英语经法语吸收。年代均为约数。

items.en: Speculari meant 'to watch from a height, to spy, to examine'. The adjective speculativus was formed on its participial stem.
items.cn: speculari 意为「从高处观察、窥探、审视」。形容词 speculativus 即在其分词词干上构成。

items.en: In later Latin, speculativus described matters belonging to contemplation rather than to action, a division inherited from Greek philosophy.
items.cn: 在晚期拉丁语中，speculativus 描述属于沉思而非行动的事物，这一区分承自希腊哲学。

items.en: Medieval schools paired speculative with practical, meaning the one seeks knowledge and the other guides conduct.
items.cn: 中世纪学校把「思辨的」与「实践的」配对，前者求知识，后者指导行为。

items.en: The adjective reached English in the fifteenth century by way of French speculatif, keeping the scholarly sense of contemplative.
items.cn: 这个形容词于 15 世纪经法语 speculatif 进入英语，保留了「沉思的」学术义。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries the same adjective was applied to ventures resting on expected prices, and the financial sense became dominant.
items.cn: 在 18 与 19 世纪，同一形容词被用于依赖预期价格的事业，金融义遂占主导。

items.en: The twentieth century added speculative fiction as a genre label and speculative application as a polite name for an unsolicited approach.
items.cn: 20 世纪又添上「推想小说」的文类标签，以及作为「主动投递」委婉说法的试探性申请。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root family and its look-alikes; group two holds adjectives that also mean uncertain or risky, with different grounds.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词族与形近词；第二组是同样表示不确定或有风险的其他形容词，各自依据不同。

entries.definition: The act or content of guessing; the adjective describes how well founded a claim or position is.
entries.definitionCN: 指猜测的动作或内容；形容词描述主张或头寸的可靠程度。

entries.definition: To form a guess or to take a price bet; the adjective is what such an act produces or embodies.
entries.definitionCN: 指作出猜测或押注价格；形容词是这样的动作产生或体现的性质。

entries.definition: The agent who speculates; the adjective does not name a person unless a noun follows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行投机的人；形容词若不接名词则不指人。

entries.definition: From spectare 'to view': striking to look at. It shares the root but not the guessing.
entries.definitionCN: 出自「观看」：指视觉上引人注目。它共享词根，但与猜测无关。

entries.definition: Resting on inference from incomplete evidence; it sounds more formal and less financial than speculative.
entries.definitionCN: 指依据不完整证据的推断；比 speculative 更书面、更少金融色彩。

entries.definition: Offered as a first attempt that may be revised; it stresses caution, not the hope of gain.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为可能修改的初次尝试；强调谨慎，而非指望收益。

entries.definition: Carrying the chance of loss; speculative adds the expectation of a reward that justifies the risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指带有损失可能；speculative 另含「有值得冒险的预期收益」。

entries.definition: Put forward as a supposition to be tested or explored; it need not involve money at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为待检验或探讨的假设提出；未必涉及金钱。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Same tower, now as a quality: whatever is seen from it is seen imperfectly, so the conclusion is a guess.
normal.cn: 同一座塔，现在化作品质：从塔上看到的东西都不完整，所以结论只是猜测。

normal.en: The family runs speculate, speculation, speculative, speculator, speculatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括推测、猜测、推测性的、投机者、凭推测地。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: speculative investment, speculative bubble, speculative fiction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：投机性投资、投机泡沫、推想小说。

normal.en: The scholarly pair is speculative and practical: one seeks truth, the other guides action.
normal.cn: 学术上的配对是「思辨的」与「实践的」：前者求真理，后者指导行动。

normal.en: A speculative application guesses that a job exists before it is advertised.
normal.cn: 试探性申请是在职位公开招聘之前就猜它存在。

abstract.en: Picture a blueprint with coins set on its corners and question marks pencilled in the margins.
abstract.cn: 想象一张蓝图，四角压着硬币，页边用铅笔写着问号。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge over fog, walked because the other side might be rich.
abstract.cn: 想象一座雾中的绳桥，人愿意走上去，只因对岸也许富庶。

abstract.en: Picture a novelist drawing a map of a country that has never existed.
abstract.cn: 想象一位小说家画出一个从未存在过的国家的地图。

examples.en: Any estimate of the storm's path this early is speculative.
examples.cn: 这么早对风暴路径作任何估计都只是推测。

examples.en: The fund attracted speculative money that vanished when rates rose.
examples.cn: 这只基金吸引了投机资金，利率上升后这些钱便消失了。

examples.en: His speculative turn of mind made him a good theorist and a poor treasurer.
examples.cn: 他爱推测的性格让他成为好的理论家、糟糕的司库。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看」的词根加形容词后缀——只凭远远看一眼就下结论，这样的结论就是推测性的；拿钱去赌这个结论就是投机性的

root: 拉丁 speculativus 出自 speculari「观察」（specula「瞭望塔」+ specere「看」），经法语 speculatif 入英语；同根词有 inspect、spectacle、perspective。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a quality rather than an act: a claim, a position, a discipline, a temperament, a genre, an approach, a price level and a motive are each said to rest on something not yet seen.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述的都是性质而非动作：主张、头寸、学科、性情、文类、接触方式、价格水平与动机，各自被说成建立在尚未看见的东西上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a conclusion built on a view from far off, with the missing part left blank.
core.cn: 核心意象：建立在远望之上的结论，缺失的部分留成空白。

branches.en: THEORY AND CONTEMPLATION: the oldest layer is a claim or a discipline that seeks truth without proof.
branches.cn: 理论与沉思：最古老的一层是求真理而无证明的主张或学科。

branches.en: MONEY AND PRICES: the guess is backed by capital, then colours a whole market level.
branches.cn: 金钱与价格：猜测由资本背书，进而染及整个市场价格水平。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same quality settles into a temperament that trusts hunches.
branches.cn: 人：同一性质沉淀为信赖直觉的性情。

branches.en: INVENTED WORLDS: imagining what does not exist is extended from markets to fiction.
branches.cn: 虚构世界：对不存在之物的想象从市场延伸到小说。

branches.en: APPROACH AND MOTIVE: an unsolicited contact and a reason to hold cash both assume a future that may not come.
branches.cn: 接触与动机：主动投递与持有现金的理由，都预设一个未必到来的未来。

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin root for looking plus a suffix meaning 'tending to'; it describes whatever leans on a view rather than on proof.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是「看」的拉丁词根加「倾向于」的后缀；它描述任何依赖视野而非证据的事物。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere 'to look' gives specula and speculari, whose adjective speculativus becomes English speculative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 specere「看」给出瞭望塔与观察，其形容词 speculativus 变成英语的 speculative。

items.example: The root is about seeing, not proving.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根关乎看见，而非证明。

items.example: The tower supplies the distance in the word.
items.exampleCN: 那座塔提供了词中的距离感。

items.example: The verb adds intent to the look.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给「看」加上意图。

items.example: Medieval schools used it for pure theory.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪学校用它指纯理论。

items.example: The noun names the act behind the quality.
items.exampleCN: 名词指这一性质背后的动作。

items.meaning: to guess; to trade on price
items.exampleCN: 他们推测下一季度的情况。

items.example: The speculator sold before the crash.
items.exampleCN: 这名投机者在崩盘前卖出。

items.meaning: tending to; of the nature of
items.example: The suffix turns an act into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成性质。

items.example: From the ridge the perspective opens.

definition_zh: 汇率；兑换比价（一种货币用另一种货币表示的价格）
definition_en: the price of one currency expressed in terms of another currency
core_image: 天平两端各放一块大小不同的砝码，中间一条刻度线标出两者的比值
scene: 签合同之前，出口商看了一眼当天的汇率，发现本币走强会把利润吃掉。Before signing, the exporter glanced at the exchange rate and saw that a stronger local currency would eat the profit.
sceneCN: 这里指「用一种货币表示另一种货币的价格」（第 1 个义项：两种货币之间的兑换比价）；句意为签合同前，出口商看了一眼当天的比价，发现本币走强会把利润吃掉。可辨识物件：天平、两块砝码、汇率牌、合同。

pos.zh: 汇率；兑换比价（可数，复数 exchange rates）

derivatives.zh: 短语的基础名词，出自拉丁「交换」→ 交换；兑换
基础名词加形容词后缀，义为「可被……」→ 可兑换的
短语的基础名词，出自拉丁「算定的份额」→ 比率；费率
与基础名词同出拉丁「计算」动词的旁系同源词 → 比率
相关词，出自拉丁「相等」→ 平价；对等
相关词，出自拉丁「转向」→ 转换；兑换

senses.title: The general price of one currency in another
senses.titleCN: 一种货币用另一种货币表示的价格
senses.definition: the number of units of one currency that must be given for one unit of another
senses.definitionCN: 为换得一单位某种货币所需付出的另一种货币的单位数
senses.example: The exchange rate moved from five to six local units per dollar in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 汇率在一个月内从每美元兑五个本币单位变为六个。
senses.why: exchange names the swap and rate names the fixed proportion, so the phrase is the proportion at which two moneys are swapped.
senses.whyCN: 兑换指交换，比率指固定的比例，整个短语就是两种货币相换时的比例。

senses.title: The rate quoted in the market at a moment
senses.titleCN: 某一时刻市场上的报价
senses.definition: the price actually available for immediate delivery, quoted continuously by dealers
senses.definitionCN: 交易商持续报出的、可即时交割的价格
senses.example: The spot exchange rate jumped within minutes of the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 声明发布后几分钟内，即期汇率就跳升了。
senses.why: dealers need a price for right now, so the general proportion becomes a live quote with a time stamp.
senses.whyCN: 交易商需要一个「此刻」的价格，于是笼统的比例变成带时间戳的实时报价。

senses.title: The official or central parity rate
senses.titleCN: 官方汇率或中心汇率
senses.definition: the reference rate published or maintained by a monetary authority
senses.definitionCN: 货币当局公布或维持的参考比价
senses.example: Customs uses the official exchange rate, not the street rate, to value imports.
senses.exampleCN: 海关用官方汇率而非街头汇率来估价进口货。
senses.why: governments need one number that applies to taxes and contracts, so a second, authoritative version of the rate appears.
senses.whyCN: 政府需要一个适用于税收与合同的统一数字，于是出现第二个具权威性的比价。

senses.title: A fixed or floating policy level
senses.titleCN: 固定或浮动制度下的汇率水平
senses.definition: the level a country chooses to defend, whether pegged or left to the market
senses.definitionCN: 一国选择守住或交由市场决定的比价水平
senses.example: A fixed exchange rate spared importers uncertainty but required large reserves.
senses.exampleCN: 固定汇率让进口商免于不确定，却需要大量储备。
senses.why: a country that pegs a rate must hold it at a chosen level, turning the number into a policy commitment.
senses.whyCN: 选择钉住汇率的国家必须把比价守在选定水平，这个数字于是变成一项政策承诺。

senses.title: The real exchange rate after price differences
senses.titleCN: 剔除物价差异后的实际汇率
senses.definition: the nominal rate adjusted for relative price levels, showing true purchasing power
senses.definitionCN: 按相对物价水平调整后的名义汇率，反映真实购买力
senses.example: Wages rose, but the real exchange rate barely moved because prices rose too.
senses.exampleCN: 工资上涨了，但因物价同样上涨，实际汇率几乎没有变动。
senses.why: price levels differ between countries, so the nominal number must be corrected before it can be compared.
senses.whyCN: 各国物价水平不同，名义数字须先做修正才能相互比较。

senses.title: The trade-weighted, or effective, rate
senses.titleCN: 按贸易权重计算的有效汇率
senses.definition: an average of several bilateral rates weighted by each partner's share of trade
senses.definitionCN: 按各贸易伙伴占比加权后若干双边汇率的平均值
senses.example: The effective exchange rate rose even though the rate against the dollar fell.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管对美元汇率下跌，有效汇率却上升了。
senses.why: one bilateral rate cannot describe trade with many partners, so an average weighted by trade is used.
senses.whyCN: 单一双边汇率无法描述与许多伙伴的贸易，于是采用按贸易加权的平均值。

senses.title: A cross rate between two other currencies
senses.titleCN: 两种第三国货币之间的交叉汇率
senses.definition: a rate between two currencies derived through a third, usually the dollar
senses.definitionCN: 通过第三种货币（通常为美元）推算出的两种货币之间的比价
senses.example: Traders quote a cross rate for the pair that never mentions the dollar.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员为这一货币对报出交叉汇率，其中根本不提美元。
senses.why: when neither currency is the dollar, dealers compute the pair through the dollar rather than quoting it directly.
senses.whyCN: 当两种货币都不是美元时，交易商通过美元推算这一货币对，而不直接报价。

senses.title: A forward rate for future delivery
senses.titleCN: 约定未来交割的远期汇率
senses.definition: a price agreed now for a currency to be delivered on a later date
senses.definitionCN: 现在约定、将来某日交割的货币价格
senses.example: The forward exchange rate was lower, which told importers what cover would cost.
senses.exampleCN: 远期汇率更低，这让进口商知道套保要花多少钱。
senses.why: a payment due later needs a price fixed now, so a second rate is created for a future date.
senses.whyCN: 将来才付的款项需要一个现在定下的价格，于是产生了为未来日期设定的第二个汇率。

senses.title: The retail rate at a counter
senses.titleCN: 柜台零售汇率
senses.definition: the rate offered to travellers and small customers, usually worse than the interbank price
senses.definitionCN: 提供给旅客与小客户的比价，通常劣于银行间价格
senses.example: The airport exchange rate was so poor that she changed only a little money.
senses.exampleCN: 机场汇率太差，她只换了一点点钱。
senses.why: a counter must cover its costs and profit, so the same rate is offered at a worse price to small buyers.
senses.whyCN: 柜台要覆盖成本与利润，于是把同一个汇率以更差的价格报给小额买者。

intro.en: Exchange comes from Latin cambiare 'to swap' by way of Old French, and rate comes from Latin rata (pars) 'a fixed share', from reri 'to reckon'. The compound is a commercial formation of the early modern period. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: exchange 经古法语上溯拉丁 cambiare「交换」，rate 来自拉丁 rata (pars)「固定的份额」，出自动词 reri「计算」。这个复合词是近代早期的商业造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cambiare meant 'to barter, to swap', used of goods as well as money. Its own earlier origin is uncertain and is usually treated as a reconstructed form.
items.cn: cambiare 意为「以物易物、交换」，既用于货物也用于钱。它更早的来源不确定，通常只作为重构形式处理。

items.en: Old French eschangier 'to exchange' carried the Latin verb into French, and English borrowed the noun and verb in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 eschangier「交换」把这个拉丁动词带进法语，英语于 14 世纪借入其名词与动词。

items.en: Rata pars meant 'a fixed, reckoned share'. The adjective ratus came from reri 'to reckon, to think', so a rate is first of all a calculated proportion.
items.cn: rata pars 意为「算定的份额」。形容词 ratus 出自动词 reri「计算、思考」，所以比率首先是算出来的比例。

items.en: English rate from the twelfth century named a fixed charge or proportion, and by the sixteenth century it was applied to the price at which one money bought another.
items.cn: 英语 rate 自 12 世纪起指固定的费用或比例，到 16 世纪已用于一种货币买另一种货币的价格。

items.en: The full phrase exchange rate is recorded in commercial writing of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, as bills of exchange made cross-border payments routine.
items.cn: 整个短语 exchange rate 见于 17 与 18 世纪的商业写作，当时汇票使跨境支付成为常规。

items.en: The twentieth century added floating rates, forward rates and trade-weighted measures, and each produced a named variety of the same number.
items.cn: 20 世纪添上浮动汇率、远期汇率与贸易加权指标，每一种都产出同一个数字的有名目的变体。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the swap root or on the reckoning root; the second holds neighbouring financial numbers that are often confused with a rate.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「交换」词根或「计算」词根的词；第二组是常与汇率混淆的相邻金融数字。

entries.definition: An older phrasing of the identical idea; the two words are simply reversed.
entries.definitionCN: 同一概念的较早说法，只是两个词的次序相反。

entries.definition: The swap itself; a rate is the proportion attached to that swap.
entries.definitionCN: 指交换行为本身；汇率是附加在这一行为上的比例。

entries.tag: a quality of goods or money
entries.definition: Able to be swapped; it says nothing about the price of the swap.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以交换；并不说明交换的价格。

entries.definition: A score or ranking; it comes from the same reckoning verb but measures merit, not money.
entries.definitionCN: 指评分或评级；同出「计算」动词，但衡量的是优劣而非金钱。

entries.definition: A declared equality between two currencies, often the anchor of a fixed regime; a rate is the actual ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 指两种货币被宣布的等值，常为固定制度的锚；汇率是实际比值。

entries.definition: The factor for changing units of one thing into another, often miles to kilometres; currency use is narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 指同一体系内单位换算的系数，常用于英里换公里；用于货币时范围更窄。

entries.definition: The charge for lending money over time; it is a price too, but of credit rather than of currency.
entries.definitionCN: 指借贷资金随时间收取的费用；它也是价格，但是信贷的价格而非货币的价格。

entries.definition: The quantity of goods one unit of money can buy; the real exchange rate compares two such powers.
entries.definitionCN: 指一单位货币能买到的货物量；实际汇率比较的正是两种这样的购买力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Exchange is the swap; rate is the reckoned proportion, so the phrase is the proportion of the swap.
normal.cn: 交换是动作，比率是算出的比例，整个短语就是交换的比例。

normal.en: The family runs exchange, exchangeable, rate, ratio, ratify: two roots, one for swapping and one for reckoning.
normal.cn: 同族词包括交换、可兑换的、比率、比值、批准：两个词根，一个管交换，一个管计算。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the regime: fixed, floating, real, effective and forward exchange rate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出制度：固定、浮动、实际、有效与远期汇率。

normal.en: A high rate against the dollar makes imports cheap and exports dear; the direction matters more than the number.
normal.cn: 对美元汇率高会让进口便宜、出口变贵；方向比数字本身更重要。

normal.en: The counter rate at an airport is the same number with a worse price for you and a margin for the seller.
normal.cn: 机场柜台汇率是同一个数字，只是对你更差、对卖方留下差价。

abstract.en: Picture two weights of different size on a balance, with the beam sliding until it settles.
abstract.cn: 想象两块大小不同的砝码放在天平上，横梁滑动直到稳定。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag written in two scripts at once, one line for each country.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签同时用两种文字写成，各为各自的国家。

abstract.en: Picture a line of ships unloading goods, each cargo priced in a different money.
abstract.cn: 想象一列船卸货，每批货物都用不同的货币标价。

examples.en: A weaker exchange rate helps exporters but raises the cost of imported fuel.
examples.cn: 汇率走弱有利于出口商，却抬高进口燃料的成本。

examples.en: The central bank defended the exchange rate by selling reserves.
examples.cn: 央行抛售储备以守住汇率。

examples.en: Tourists rarely notice the difference between the official and the street exchange rate.
examples.cn: 游客很少注意到官方汇率与街头汇率的差别。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「交换」加「比率」——两种钱相换时按什么比例换，这个比例就是汇率

root: exchange 经古法语上溯拉丁 cambiare「交换」，更深来源不确定；rate 来自拉丁 rata (pars)「算定的份额」，出自动词 reri「计算」，同根有 ratio、ratify。短语成形于 17 至 18 世纪的商业写作。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses are one number seen from nine positions: the general proportion, the live quote, the official figure, the defended level, the real and weighted versions, the cross and forward versions, and the counter price for a traveller.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项是同一个数字的九种立场：笼统比例、实时报价、官方数字、被守住的水平、实际与加权版本、交叉与远期版本，以及旅客在柜台看到的价格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance beam settles at a proportion that both sides accept.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平横梁停在一个双方都接受的比例上。

branches.en: FROM THE GENERAL TO THE COUNTER: the plain proportion and the retail price are the two ends of the same scale.
branches.cn: 从笼统到柜台：朴素的比例与零售价格是同一刻度的两端。

branches.en: MARKET AND AUTHORITY: a live quote and an official reference answer the same question from opposite sides.
branches.cn: 市场与权威：实时报价与官方参考从两侧回答同一个问题。

branches.en: POLICY LEVEL: a government decides whether to hold the number still or let it move.
branches.cn: 政策水平：政府决定把这个数字按住还是放开。

branches.en: ADJUSTED VIEWS: subtracting price effects, or averaging by trade weight, changes what the number means.
branches.cn: 调整后的视角：剔除物价影响，或按贸易加权，改变了数字的含义。

branches.en: DERIVED AND FUTURE RATES: one is computed through a third currency, the other is fixed for a later date.
branches.cn: 推算与远期：一个透过第三种货币算出，另一个为将来的日期定下。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin verb for swapping with a Latin noun for a reckoned share; neither half is an affix, but each is a root with its own family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把表示「交换」的拉丁动词与表示「算定份额」的拉丁名词连在一起；两半都不是词缀，而是各有词族的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin cambiare stands behind exchange; Latin rata pars and reri stand behind rate, ratio and ratify.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cambiare 支撑 exchange 一族；拉丁 rata pars 与 reri 支撑 rate、ratio 与 ratify 一族。

items.example: The voucher is exchangeable for goods.
She had no change for the bus.
The rate is set each morning.
items.exampleCN: 这个比率每天早上定一次。

items.example: The ratio of debt to income rose.
items.exampleCN: 债务与收入的比值上升了。

items.example: The agency cut the country's rating.
items.exampleCN: 评级机构下调了该国评级。

items.example: The two currencies were kept at parity.
items.exampleCN: 两种货币被维持在平价。

definition_zh: 外汇；外币；（银行间的）外汇交易与外汇市场
definition_en: money held in currencies other than one's own, and the market and business of trading such money
core_image: 一只透明匣子里叠着几种颜色不同的纸币，匣盖贴着一张换算表
scene: 这家小厂把海外的货款汇回本国，必须先到银行办理外汇结算。The small factory had to settle its foreign exchange at the bank before the overseas payment could reach its account.
sceneCN: 这里指「以外国货币计价的资金及其结算往来」（第 1 个义项：本国货币之外的货币资金）；句意为这家小厂把海外货款汇回本国，必须先到银行办理外汇结算。可辨识物件：外币纸币、换算表、银行柜台、结算单。

pos.zh: 外汇；外币（不可数；作为业务时可指外汇交易）
作定语：外汇的（如外汇储备、外汇市场）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多笔外汇业务）

短语的基础形容词，义为「门外的」→ 外国的
基础形容词加表示人的后缀 → 外国人
短语的基础名词，出自拉丁「交换」→ 交换；兑换
基础名词加形容词后缀，义为「可被……」→ 可兑换的

senses.title: Money held in other countries' currencies
senses.titleCN: 以他国货币持有的资金
senses.definition: currency that is not the legal tender of the holder's own country
senses.definitionCN: 非持有者本国法定货币的货币
senses.example: The exporter kept part of its earnings in foreign exchange rather than converting at once.
senses.exampleCN: 出口商把部分收入以外汇形式留存，没有立即兑换。
senses.why: foreign marks what is outside the home currency, and exchange marks the swap, so the phrase names money that must be swapped before it can be used at home.
senses.whyCN: 「外国的」标出本国货币之外，「交换」标出兑换，整个短语指必须先换过才能在国内使用的钱。

senses.title: The interbank currency market
senses.titleCN: 银行间的外汇市场
senses.definition: the global network of dealers and platforms where currencies are bought and sold
senses.definitionCN: 交易商与平台在全球买卖货币的网络
senses.example: Turnover in foreign exchange exceeds that of every other financial market.
senses.exampleCN: 外汇市场的成交额超过其他任何金融市场。
senses.why: many dealers and platforms quote at once, so the sum of their trades becomes a market rather than a single swap.
senses.whyCN: 许多交易商与平台同时报价，他们交易的总和于是成为一个市场，而非一次单独的交换。

senses.title: Reserves held by a monetary authority
senses.titleCN: 货币当局持有的外汇储备
senses.definition: the stock of foreign currency and claims a central bank keeps to defend its own money
senses.definitionCN: 中央银行为捍卫本国货币而持有的外币与债权存量
senses.example: The bank spent a fifth of its foreign exchange to slow the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 该央行动用了五分之一的外汇储备来减缓跌势。
senses.why: a central bank must hold foreign money to intervene, so the phrase also names the stock it keeps.
senses.whyCN: 央行必须持有外国货币才能干预，因此这个短语也指它所存的存量。

senses.title: A settlement or conversion transaction
senses.titleCN: 一笔外汇结算或兑换
senses.definition: the actual operation of buying, selling or settling a foreign currency payment
senses.definitionCN: 买入、卖出或结算外币支付的实际操作
senses.example: The invoice was settled by a foreign exchange transfer through two banks.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔发票通过两家银行的外汇转账结算。
senses.why: the abstract money becomes a concrete operation when an invoice has to be paid across a border.
senses.whyCN: 当一张发票需要跨境支付时，抽象的外币就变成一次具体操作。

senses.title: Earnings received in foreign currency
senses.titleCN: 以外币取得的收入
senses.definition: export revenue or other income that arrives in a currency other than the home one
senses.definitionCN: 以非本国货币到账的出口收入或其他收入
senses.example: Tourism is the island's main source of foreign exchange.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业是该岛主要的外汇收入来源。
senses.why: exporters and hosts receive payment in the buyer's currency, so the phrase also names the inflow.
senses.whyCN: 出口商与接待方收取买方货币的付款，因此这个短语也指流入的那一笔。

senses.title: Exposure to currency movements
senses.titleCN: 承受汇率变动的敞口
senses.definition: the risk that a change in currency values alters the value of a payment or holding
senses.definitionCN: 货币价值变化改变某笔支付或持有物价值的风险
senses.example: A firm with costs at home and sales abroad carries constant foreign exchange risk.
senses.exampleCN: 成本在本国、销售在国外的公司长期承担外汇风险。
senses.why: holding or owing foreign money means a price move can change the value of the position.
senses.whyCN: 持有或欠下外币，意味着价格变动能改变头寸的价值。

senses.title: Official control of currency dealings
senses.titleCN: 官方对外汇往来的管制
senses.definition: rules that limit who may hold or trade foreign currency and at what rate
senses.definitionCN: 限制何人可持有或交易外币以及按何价的规则
senses.example: During the shortage, foreign exchange was rationed by licence.
senses.exampleCN: 在短缺时期，外汇凭许可证配给。
senses.why: a state short of foreign money may forbid or license its use, which adds a legal sense.
senses.whyCN: 缺少外汇的国家可能禁止或凭许可使用它，于是添上法律义。

senses.title: A retail counter that sells currency
senses.titleCN: 出售外币的零售柜台
senses.definition: a shop or desk where travellers buy and sell foreign notes
senses.definitionCN: 旅客买卖外币现钞的店铺或柜台
senses.example: She bought euros at a foreign exchange near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在车站附近的一家外币兑换点买了欧元。
senses.why: travellers need notes in hand, so the same business appears as a counter selling paper money.
senses.whyCN: 旅客需要手头的现钞，同一业务于是表现为出售纸币的柜台。

intro.en: Foreign descends from Latin foris 'outside', by way of foranus and Old French forain; exchange comes from Latin cambiare 'to swap'. The phrase is a commercial formation of the early modern period. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: foreign 经拉丁 foranus 与古法语 forain 上溯 foris「外面」；exchange 出自拉丁 cambiare「交换」。这个短语是近代早期的商业造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Foris meant 'outside, out of doors', and it also underlies forum, the open space outside a house. What is foreign is literally what is outside the door.
items.cn: foris 意为「外面、户外」，也是 forum（屋外空地）的来源。所谓外国的，字面上就是门外的。

items.en: The adjective foranus 'of the outside' passed into Old French as forain, and English took it as foreign in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 形容词 foranus「外面的」进入古法语作 forain，英语于 15 世纪吸收为 foreign。

items.en: Cambiare 'to barter, swap' gave Old French eschangier and English exchange; its own earlier origin is uncertain and is treated as reconstructed.
items.cn: cambiare「以物易物、交换」给出古法语 eschangier 与英语 exchange；它更早的来源不确定，按重构处理。

items.en: From the fourteenth century, a bill of exchange let a merchant pay abroad without carrying coin, and foreign exchange grew out of that trade.
items.cn: 自 14 世纪起，汇票让商人无需携带硬币即可在海外付款，外汇业务正是从这种贸易中生长出来。

items.en: The phrase foreign exchange is recorded from the seventeenth century, first for foreign bills and coin, later for the market that trades them.
items.cn: 短语 foreign exchange 见于 17 世纪，先指外国汇票与硬币，后指交易它们的市场。

items.en: The twentieth century added reserves, controls, risk and a global interbank market, each with its own vocabulary.
items.cn: 20 世纪添上储备、管制、风险与全球银行间市场，每一项都有自己的说法。

note.en: Group one holds words built on outside or on swapping; group two holds related financial terms that name other parts of the same system.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「外面」或「交换」词根的词；第二组是同一体系内指其他环节的金融术语。

entries.definition: A person from another country; the money sense belongs to the phrase, not to this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指来自另一国的人；货币义属于短语，而不属于这个名词。

entries.definition: A traders' shortening of the phrase, used mainly for the market rather than for banknotes.
entries.definitionCN: 交易员对短语的缩略，主要指标市场而非现钞。

entries.definition: The swap of one thing for another; adding foreign specifies that the things are currencies.
entries.definitionCN: 指一物换一物的动作；加上「外国的」才限定所换之物为货币。

entries.definition: The proportion at which two currencies swap; foreign exchange is the money and the business itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指两种货币相换的比例；外汇则是货币本身与业务本身。

entries.definition: Foreign money from a politically and economically stable country, easily accepted in trade.
entries.definitionCN: 指来自政治经济稳定国家、贸易中易被接受的外币，是外汇的一部分。

entries.definition: Money sent by a worker abroad to family at home; it is a flow of foreign exchange, not the whole stock.
entries.definitionCN: 指在外工作者寄回家人的钱；它是外汇的一种流量，而非全部存量。

entries.tag: money crossing borders for any purpose
entries.definition: Movement of investment money across borders; currency exchange may or may not be involved.
entries.definitionCN: 指投资资金跨境流动；未必涉及货币兑换。

entries.definition: The national ledger of all cross-border payments; foreign exchange dealings are one line inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 指一国全部跨境支付的账簿；外汇往来只是其中一行。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Foreign means outside the door; exchange means swap: money from outside that must be swapped.
normal.cn: 「外国的」指门外，「交换」指换，合起来就是门外来的、必须换过才能用的钱。

normal.en: The family runs foreign, foreigner, exchange, exchangeable, forex.
normal.cn: 同族词包括外国的、外国人、交换、可兑换的、外汇缩略语。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the parts of the system: market, reserves, earnings, control, risk.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出体系的各部分：市场、储备、收入、管制、风险。

normal.en: A bill of exchange let a merchant pay abroad without carrying coin, which is where the business began.
normal.cn: 汇票让商人不必携带硬币就能在海外付款，业务正是从这里开始。

normal.en: Reserves are the country's saved foreign money, kept for the day its own currency needs defending.
normal.cn: 外汇储备是国家存下的外币，留着在本国货币需要捍卫的那天使用。

abstract.en: Picture a glass box holding several colours of paper money, with a conversion chart on the lid.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃匣装几种颜色的纸币，盖子上贴着换算表。

abstract.en: Picture a merchant in one port paying a supplier in another, with no coin travelling between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个港口的商人向另一港口的供货商付款，硬币并未在两地之间移动。

abstract.en: Picture a country's vault of foreign notes, counted each month against its own currency.
abstract.cn: 想象一国存外币的金库，每月对着本国货币盘点一次。

examples.en: The country earns most of its foreign exchange from tourism and remittances.
examples.cn: 该国的外汇收入大部分来自旅游与侨汇。

examples.en: Foreign exchange desks in the capital reported unusually heavy selling of the local currency.
examples.cn: 首都的外汇柜台报告本币出现异常大量的卖盘。

examples.en: Controls on foreign exchange made it hard for firms to pay overseas suppliers.
examples.cn: 外汇管制让企业难以向海外供货商付款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外国的」加「交换」——从门外来的钱，用之前先得换成本国货币 → 外汇

root: foreign 经拉丁 foranus 上溯 foris「外面」，与 forum 同源；exchange 出自拉丁 cambiare「交换」，更深来源不确定。短语成形于 17 世纪，源自汇票贸易。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: money crosses a border, must be swapped, is traded in a market, is stored as reserves, settles an invoice, arrives as earnings, creates risk, is controlled, and is sold at a counter.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个流动展开：钱越过边界，必须被交换，在市场中被交易，被存成储备，结算一张发票，作为收入到账，产生风险，受到管制，最后在柜台上被卖出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: currency from outside the door, waiting to be swapped before it can be spent at home.
core.cn: 核心意象：从门外来的货币，换过之后才能在国内花用。

branches.en: THE MONEY AND THE OPERATION: the stock of outside currency and the act of settling it.
branches.cn: 货币与操作：门外货币的存量，以及结算它的动作。

branches.en: THE MARKET: dealers meet to swap one currency for another at quoted prices.
branches.cn: 市场：交易商按报价把一种货币换成另一种。

branches.en: THE STATE'S HAND: reserves are what the state keeps, controls are what it forbids.
branches.cn: 国家之手：储备是国家留下的，管制是国家禁止的。

branches.en: INFLOW AND EXPOSURE: money arrives as earnings, and the same flow exposes the holder to price moves.
branches.cn: 流入与敞口：钱作为收入到账，同一流动又让持有者承受价格变动。

branches.en: THE COUNTER: the same money appears as banknotes sold to a traveller.
branches.cn: 柜台：同一笔钱以现钞形式卖给旅客。

intro.en: Both halves are old borrowings: one from a Latin word for outside, one from a Latin verb for swapping, and each brought a family of English words with it.
intro.cn: 两半都是古老借词：一半来自拉丁语「外面」，一半来自拉丁语「交换」，各自带来一族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin foris and foranus stand behind foreign; Latin cambiare stands behind exchange, change and interchangeable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 foris 与 foranus 支撑 foreign 一族；拉丁 cambiare 支撑 exchange、change 与 interchangeable。

items.exampleCN: 一位外国人开了这家店。

items.example: The accent gave a faint foreignness.
items.exampleCN: 口音带来一点外来的感觉。

items.example: The note is exchangeable at any branch.
items.exampleCN: 这张票据可在任何分行兑换。

items.meaning: able to stand in for each other

items.example: He gave her the wrong change.

definition_zh: 货币政策（中央银行通过利率、货币供应与信贷条件调节经济的措施）
definition_en: the set of actions by which a central bank controls the money supply, credit and interest rates
core_image: 一只大阀门接在贯穿全城的水管上，阀门前站着一个佩官方徽章的人
scene: 通胀连续三个月高于目标，央行行长在例会上主张收紧货币政策。With inflation above target for a third month, the governor argued for tighter monetary policy.
sceneCN: 这里指「中央银行调节货币与信贷条件的整套措施」（第 1 个义项：用利率与货币供应影响整体经济）；句意为通胀连续三个月高于目标，行长在例会上主张收紧货币政策。可辨识物件：阀门、水管、通胀曲线、会议桌。

pos.zh: 货币政策（不可数）
作定语：货币政策的（如政策委员会）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多国各自的政策）

derivatives.zh: 短语的基础形容词，出自拉丁「铸币厂的」→ 货币的
与基础形容词同出罗马铸币女神之名的同源词 → 钱
基础形容词词干加动词后缀，义为「使成为」→ 货币化
短语的基础名词，经拉丁上溯希腊「城邦治理」→ 政策
基础名词加表示制定者的复合成分 → 决策者

senses.title: The central bank's overall stance
senses.titleCN: 中央银行的总立场
senses.definition: the general direction a central bank takes in managing money and credit
senses.definitionCN: 中央银行在管理货币与信贷时采取的总方向
senses.example: Monetary policy was described as mildly restrictive in the quarterly report.
senses.exampleCN: 季度报告把货币政策形容为轻度限制性。
senses.why: monetary marks the object, money and credit, while policy marks a deliberate course, so the phrase is a chosen course about money.
senses.whyCN: 「货币的」标出对象是货币与信贷，「政策」标出有意选定的路线，合起来就是关于货币的既定路线。

senses.title: Easy or expansionary policy
senses.titleCN: 宽松或扩张性政策
senses.definition: a stance that lowers rates and adds money to encourage borrowing and spending
senses.definitionCN: 降低利率并增加货币以鼓励借贷与支出的立场
senses.example: Easy monetary policy kept mortgage payments low for years.
senses.exampleCN: 宽松的货币政策让房贷还款在多年里保持低位。
senses.why: easy names what borrowers feel: money is made cheap and plentiful, so the valve is opened.
senses.whyCN: 「宽松」说的是借款人的感受：钱变得便宜而充足，阀门被打开。

senses.title: Tight or contractionary policy
senses.titleCN: 紧缩或限制性政策
senses.definition: a stance that raises rates and restricts credit in order to cool demand and inflation
senses.definitionCN: 提高利率并限制信贷，以压低需求与通胀的立场
senses.example: Tight monetary policy slowed hiring within two quarters.
senses.exampleCN: 紧缩的货币政策在两个月季度内就放缓了招聘。
senses.why: tight names the same valve turned the other way: money is made dear and scarce.
senses.whyCN: 「紧缩」指同一阀门朝反方向拧：钱变得昂贵而稀缺。

senses.title: Setting the policy rate
senses.titleCN: 设定政策利率
senses.definition: the regular decision about the rate at which the central bank lends or the target for market rates
senses.definitionCN: 中央银行定期决定拆借利率或市场利率目标的动作
senses.example: The committee raised the policy rate by half a point.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会把政策利率提高了半个百分点。
senses.why: the rate is the one number the bank can announce, so the whole stance is often read through it.
senses.whyCN: 利率是央行唯一能公布的数字，整套立场常被透过它来解读。

senses.title: Controlling money and credit growth
senses.titleCN: 控制货币与信贷的增长
senses.definition: the older task of limiting how much money and bank lending expand
senses.definitionCN: 限制货币与银行贷款扩张规模的较早任务
senses.example: In the postwar decades, monetary policy meant chiefly guarding the money supply.
senses.exampleCN: 战后几十年里，货币政策主要指看住货币供应量。
senses.why: before rate policy, the quantity of money itself was the target, and the older sense still survives.
senses.whyCN: 在利率政策之前，被瞄准的是货币数量本身，这个较早的义项至今仍在。

senses.title: Unconventional measures
senses.titleCN: 非常规措施
senses.definition: tools used when rates are near zero, such as large asset purchases and forward guidance
senses.definitionCN: 在利率近零时使用的工具，如大规模购买资产与前瞻性指引
senses.example: After rates hit zero, monetary policy turned to buying bonds in bulk.
senses.exampleCN: 利率触零之后，货币政策转向大量购买债券。
senses.why: when the ordinary lever cannot go lower, the bank must buy assets or promise future action.
senses.whyCN: 当寻常杠杆无法再低时，央行只能购买资产或承诺未来行动。

senses.title: An inflation-targeting framework
senses.titleCN: 通胀目标框架
senses.definition: a rule-bound system in which the bank publicly commits to a numerical inflation target
senses.definitionCN: 中央银行公开承诺一个数字通胀目标的规则化体系
senses.example: The country adopted inflation targeting as the core of its monetary policy in the 1990s.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在 20 世纪 90 年代把通胀目标制作为货币政策的核心。
senses.why: a public number gives the market a rule to expect, which is why the framework became a sense of its own.
senses.whyCN: 公开的数字给市场一条可预期的规则，这一框架因此成为一个独立义项。

senses.title: Transmission to bank lending
senses.titleCN: 向银行贷款的传导
senses.definition: the way a rate decision reaches mortgages, business loans and finally prices and jobs
senses.definitionCN: 利率决定如何传到房贷、企业贷款，最终传到物价与就业
senses.example: Economists study how fast monetary policy transmits to small business credit.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家研究货币政策多快能传导到小企业信贷。
senses.why: a decision only matters if it reaches mortgages and payrolls, so economists study that path as part of the policy.
senses.whyCN: 决定只有传到房贷与工资才起作用，经济学家于是把这条路径也算作政策的一部分。

senses.title: Coordination with fiscal policy
senses.titleCN: 与财政政策的配合
senses.definition: the division of labour between the central bank and the government's budget
senses.definitionCN: 中央银行与政府预算之间的分工
senses.example: When the budget is loose, monetary policy may have to be tighter than it would like.
senses.exampleCN: 预算宽松时，货币政策可能不得不比它本意更紧。
senses.why: the bank and the treasury share one economy, so their two courses must be set with each other in view.
senses.whyCN: 央行与财政部共用同一个经济，两条路线必须相互参照着定。

intro.en: Monetary comes from Latin monetarius, from moneta 'mint, money', and policy from Greek politeia 'citizenship, government' by way of Latin politia and French. The compound belongs to twentieth-century central banking. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monetary 来自拉丁 monetarius，其根 moneta 意为「铸币厂、货币」；policy 经拉丁 politia 与法语上溯希腊 politeia「公民身份、治理」。这个复合词属于 20 世纪的中央银行实践。年代均为约数。

items.en: Moneta was a name of a goddess whose temple in Rome housed the mint, so the word shifted from the goddess to the place of coining and then to the coin itself.
items.cn: moneta 原是一位女神的名字，她在罗马的神庙中设有铸币厂，词义遂从女神转到铸币之地，再转到钱本身。

items.en: The adjective monetarius meant 'of the mint or of coinage', and English monetary entered through it in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 形容词 monetarius 意为「铸币厂的、铸币的」，英语 monetary 于 17 世纪经它进入。

items.en: Greek polis 'city' gave politeia, the condition and business of being a citizen, from which the idea of a settled way of governing grew.
items.cn: 希腊 polis「城邦」给出 politeia，即公民的身份与事务，由此生长出「既定治理方式」的观念。

items.en: Latin politia rendered the Greek noun, and Old French policie carried it toward English policy, first as government and later as a chosen course of action.
items.cn: 拉丁 politia 转写这一希腊名词，古法语 policie 把它带向英语 policy，先指治理，后指选定的行动路线。

items.en: By the fifteenth century policy meant a system of government; the broader sense of any deliberate plan appears later.
items.cn: 到 15 世纪，policy 指治理体系；任何有意计划的宽泛义则出现得更晚。

items.en: Monetary policy became a standard term in the twentieth century, as central banks were given explicit responsibility for money and credit.
items.cn: 货币政策在 20 世纪成为标准术语，当时中央银行被明确赋予管理货币与信贷的职责。

note.en: Group one holds words built on money or on government; group two holds policies and instruments that are often put beside it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「货币」或「治理」词根的词；第二组是常与之并列的政策与工具。

entries.definition: Relating to money or currency; the full phrase adds that a deliberate course is being chosen.
entries.definitionCN: 指与货币有关；整个短语另含「正在选定一条路线」。

entries.definition: To convert something into money or to coin it; it names an action, not a policy stance.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物转为货币或铸币；它指动作，而非政策立场。

entries.definition: A settled course of action; on its own it could concern health, trade or anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 指既定的行动路线；单独使用时可以指卫生、贸易等任何领域。

entries.definition: The activity of competing for power; policy is the settled course that follows from it.
entries.definitionCN: 指争夺权力的活动；政策是由此形成的既定路线。

entries.definition: Taxing and spending by the government; monetary policy works through money and credit instead.
entries.definitionCN: 指政府的征税与支出；货币政策则通过货币与信贷起作用。

entries.definition: The use of the policy rate alone; monetary policy also covers asset purchases and guidance.
entries.definitionCN: 指单用政策利率；货币政策还包括购买资产与指引。

entries.definition: Deliberate management of the currency's external price rather than of domestic credit.
entries.definitionCN: 指有意管理货币的对外价格，而非国内信贷。

entries.definition: Binding rules on how banks may behave; monetary policy tries to influence demand, not to prescribe conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 指约束银行行为的规则；货币政策试图影响需求，而非规定行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Monetary points at money; policy points at a chosen course, so the phrase is a chosen course about money and credit.
normal.cn: 「货币的」指向钱，「政策」指向选定的路线，合起来就是关于货币与信贷的既定路线。

normal.en: The family runs money, monetary, monetize, policy, policymaker, politics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括钱、货币的、货币化、政策、政策制定者、政治。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the stance: tight, loose, restrictive and accommodative monetary policy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出立场：紧缩、宽松、限制性与适应性货币政策。

normal.en: The mint stands inside the word: Moneta was the temple where Rome coined its money.
normal.cn: 铸币厂就在词里：罗马的摩涅塔神庙里曾设铸币厂。

normal.en: Two levers exist: the central bank pulls the money lever, the treasury pulls the tax-and-spend lever.
normal.cn: 有两根杠杆：央行拉货币那根，财政部拉税收与支出那根。

abstract.en: Picture one large valve on a pipe that feeds the whole city, with a badged hand on the wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象一根向全城供水的水管上只有一只大阀门，一只佩戴徽章的手握着转轮。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat set to a number, and a committee arguing about whether to turn it down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只设定到某个数字的恒温器，一群人正在争论要不要调低。

abstract.en: Picture a river that can be widened or narrowed, and fields on both banks waiting for the level.
abstract.cn: 想象一条可被放宽或收窄的河，两岸的田地都在等水位。

examples.en: Monetary policy cannot build factories, but it can decide how expensive it is to borrow for one.
examples.cn: 货币政策建不了工厂，却能决定借钱建厂有多贵。

examples.en: The bank published its monetary policy report on the same day as the rate decision.
examples.cn: 央行在公布利率决定的同一天发布了货币政策报告。

examples.en: When the exchange rate is fixed, monetary policy loses much of its freedom.
examples.cn: 汇率被固定时，货币政策会失去很大一部分自由。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「货币」加「政策」——央行握着货币这根管子上的阀门，决定钱多钱少、借钱贵不贵 → 货币政策

root: monetary 来自拉丁 monetarius，其根 moneta「铸币厂、货币」源自在罗马神庙中设铸币厂的女神名；policy 经拉丁 politia 与古法语上溯希腊 politeia「公民身份、治理」，根为 polis「城邦」。复合术语成形于 20 世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run one lever: an overall stance, two directions, a rate decision, control of money and credit, tools for when rates hit zero, a target framework, transmission to real borrowers, and coordination with the budget.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一根杠杆：总立场、两个方向、一次利率决定、对货币与信贷的控制、利率触零时的工具、目标框架、向真实借款人的传导，以及与预算的配合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one valve on the pipe that feeds the whole economy.
core.cn: 核心意象：向整个经济供水的水管上的一只阀门。

branches.en: STANCE AND DIRECTION: the same course can be described as a whole, or as loosening and tightening.
branches.cn: 立场与方向：同一条路线可整体描述，也可拆成放松与收紧。

branches.en: THE POLICY RATE: one number is decided at intervals and announced to the market.
branches.cn: 政策利率：一个数字被定期决定，并向市场公布。

branches.en: THE OLDER TASK: before rates were the main tool, the quantity of money itself was guarded.
branches.cn: 较早的任务：在利率成为主要工具之前，被看住的是货币数量本身。

branches.en: WHEN THE TOOL FAILS: near zero, buying assets and setting a target replace the ordinary lever.
branches.cn: 工具失灵时：利率近零，购买资产与设定目标取代寻常杠杆。

branches.en: OUT INTO THE ECONOMY: the decision reaches borrowers, and must share the field with the budget.
branches.cn: 进入经济：决定传到借款人，并须与预算共用同一场地。

intro.en: Two borrowings are joined: a Latin adjective for coinage and a Greek-derived noun for a governing course. Each half still carries its own family.
intro.cn: 两个借词相连：一个表示铸币的拉丁形容词，一个源自希腊语、表示治理路线的名词。两半各自仍带词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin moneta and monetarius stand behind the money half; Latin politia, from Greek politeia, stands behind the policy half.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 moneta 与 monetarius 支撑「货币」这一半；拉丁 politia（源自希腊 politeia）支撑「政策」这一半。

items.meaning: the act of converting into money
items.exampleCN: 债务货币化让投资者担忧。

items.meaning: the place where coin is made

items.example: The policy takes effect in June.
A small polity can act quickly.
items.exampleCN: 小的政治共同体能迅速行动。

latinEntries.structure: politia, -ae (f., first declension, from Greek politeia)

definition_zh: 财政的；政府收支与税收的；（苏格兰、西班牙等）检察官的
definition_en: relating to government money, especially taxes and public spending
core_image: 一只公家的钱箱，进账口贴着税单，出账口接向街道的公共工程

sceneCN: 这里指「与政府收支及税收有关的」（第 1 个义项：属于国家财政收入与支出的事务）；句意为预算草案把新增收入全部投向乡镇诊所，财政官员称这是本年度最优先的支出。可辨识物件：钱箱、税单、诊所图纸、预算册。

（苏格兰、西班牙等）检察官；财政官员

基础形容词加副词后缀 → 在财政上
