senses.title: Relating to government revenue and spending
senses.titleCN: 与政府收入及支出有关
senses.definition: concerning the money a government raises through taxes and spends on public needs
senses.definitionCN: 关于政府以税收取得、并用于公共需要的钱
senses.example: The fiscal cost of the programme was spread over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划的财政成本被分摊到十年之间。
senses.why: the word descends from the Latin word for a money basket, so whatever is fiscal belongs to the public purse rather than a private one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词上溯拉丁语中「钱筐」的说法，因此凡是财政的，都属公家钱袋而非私人钱包。

senses.title: The twelve-month accounting period
senses.titleCN: 财政年度这一十二个月的账期
senses.definition: the year a government or firm uses for budgeting and accounts, which need not begin in January
senses.definitionCN: 政府或企业用于预算与记账的年度，未必从一月开始
senses.example: The fiscal year closes at the end of March for many public bodies.
senses.exampleCN: 许多公共机构的财政年度在三月底结束。
senses.why: because accounts must be closed somewhere, the adjective attaches to the period chosen, giving a fixed label to an arbitrary calendar span.
senses.whyCN: 账目总要在某处结清，这个形容词于是附着在被选定的期间上，为一个任意的日历跨度提供固定标签。

senses.title: The balance of the public budget
senses.titleCN: 公共预算的收支状况
senses.definition: describing whether a government is running a surplus, a balance or a deficit
senses.definitionCN: 描述政府处于盈余、平衡还是赤字状态
senses.example: The country entered the crisis with a fiscal surplus of two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 该国带着相当于经济总量百分之二的财政盈余进入危机。
senses.why: once taxes and spending are counted, the difference is a fact about the public purse, so the adjective names the state of that balance.
senses.whyCN: 税收与支出算清之后，差额成为公家钱袋的事实，这个形容词便指该差额的状态。

senses.title: Fiscal discipline and restraint
senses.titleCN: 财政纪律与自我约束
senses.definition: the practice of keeping spending and borrowing inside agreed limits
senses.definitionCN: 把支出与借款保持在约定限度内的做法
senses.example: Fiscal discipline required the ministry to refuse the extra request.
senses.exampleCN: 财政纪律要求该部拒绝这笔额外申请。
senses.why: the word can be pressed into service as a norm, not only a description, which is why it appears beside discipline and restraint.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以被当作规范使用，而不只是描述，因此常与纪律、约束一类词并置。

senses.title: Fiscal stimulus by spending or cutting tax
senses.titleCN: 以增支或减税作财政刺激
senses.definition: a deliberate expansion of the budget to raise demand during a slowdown
senses.definitionCN: 在放缓时期有意扩大预算以提高需求
senses.example: The fiscal stimulus arrived late but was large enough to shorten the recession.
senses.exampleCN: 财政刺激来得迟，但规模足以缩短衰退。
senses.why: when private demand falls, the public budget can take its place for a season, so extra spending is the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 私人需求下滑时，公共预算可以暂时替代它，额外支出于是成为工具。

senses.title: The fiscal burden on taxpayers
senses.titleCN: 纳税人承受的财政负担
senses.definition: the weight of taxes and contributions that households and firms must carry
senses.definitionCN: 家庭与企业必须承担的税收与缴费之重
senses.example: Officials argued that the fiscal burden already discouraged hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 官员认为财政负担已经在抑制招聘。
senses.why: every tax is a claim on private income, so the same budget that funds services also weighs on those who pay.
senses.whyCN: 每一项税都是对私人收入的索取，因此供给公共服务的同一预算也压在被征者身上。

senses.title: A revenue stamp or fiscal mark
senses.titleCN: 印花税票或财政标记
senses.definition: an official stamp showing that a tax on a document has been paid
senses.definitionCN: 表明某份文书已缴税的官方印花
senses.example: The deed carried a fiscal stamp in the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据的角上贴着财政印花。
senses.why: taxing papers required a visible proof of payment, so the adjective came to name the mark as well as the treasury behind it.
senses.whyCN: 对文书征税需要看得见的缴款凭证，这个形容词于是既指国库，也指那个印记。

senses.title: A public prosecutor in some legal systems
senses.titleCN: 某些法系中的检察官
senses.definition: the official who prosecutes on behalf of the state, as in Scots and Spanish practice
senses.definitionCN: 代表国家提起公诉的官员，如苏格兰与西班牙的用法
senses.example: The fiscal presented the evidence to the court.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官向法庭提交了证据。
senses.why: the prosecutor was originally the treasury's lawyer, so the same word for the purse produced a title for the state's advocate.
senses.whyCN: 检察官最初是国库的律师，因此同一个表示钱袋的词也产出了国家公诉人的头衔。

intro.en: Fiscal comes from Latin fiscalis 'of the fiscus', the basket or chest that held public money. English borrowed it through French in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fiscal 来自拉丁 fiscalis「属于 fiscus 的」，fiscus 原指盛公款的篮子或钱箱。英语于 16 世纪经法语借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fiscus first meant a woven basket, then the chest in which the Roman treasury kept its money, and finally the treasury itself as an institution.
items.cn: fiscus 先指编织的篮子，后指罗马国库存放钱款的钱箱，最后指作为机构的国库本身。

items.en: The adjective fiscalis 'of the treasury' described officials, taxes and property belonging to the public chest rather than to the emperor's private purse.
items.cn: 形容词 fiscalis「国库的」描述属于公家钱箱而非皇帝私产的官员、税收与财物。

items.en: Old French fiscal carried the word into English in the sixteenth century, at first in legal writing about the royal treasury.
items.cn: 古法语 fiscal 于 16 世纪把这个词带进英语，最初见于关于王室国库的法律文书。

items.en: By the eighteenth century fiscal was used broadly for taxes, debt and budgeting, and the phrase fiscal year took its modern meaning in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，fiscal 已广泛用于税收、债务与预算；「财政年度」一语在 19 世纪取得现代含义。

items.en: In legal systems where the state's advocate acted for the treasury, fiscal became a title for the public prosecutor, a sense still current in Scotland and Spain.
items.cn: 在国家公诉人代国库行事的法系中，fiscal 成为检察官的头衔，这一义在苏格兰与西班牙仍在使用。

items.en: The revenue stamp sense arose because a taxed document needed a visible mark, so the adjective named the proof of payment as well as the office behind it.
items.cn: 印花义的产生，是因为被征税的文书需要看得见的标记，形容词于是既指缴款凭证，也指其背后的机关。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words from the treasury root or the same budget field; group two holds adjectives that are often used where fiscal belongs.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「国库」词根或同属预算领域的形近词；第二组是常被用在 fiscal 位置上的其他形容词。

entries.definition: The treasury or public purse itself, an archaic noun; fiscal describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指国库或公家钱袋本身，是古旧名词；fiscal 描述属于它的事物。

entries.definition: In financial terms, especially of public money; it modifies an action rather than naming a field.
entries.definitionCN: 指从财政角度，尤指公款；它修饰动作，而非命名领域。

entries.definition: To take property into the public chest as a penalty; the root is the same money basket.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为处罚把财物收进公家钱箱；词根正是那只钱筐。

entries.definition: Relating to the body or to matter, from a different Greek root; it shares only a sound.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体的或物质的，出自另一希腊词根；仅读音相近。

entries.definition: Relating to money and finance in general, including private firms; fiscal is reserved for public money.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指金钱与金融，包含私人企业；fiscal 专指公款。

entries.definition: Relating to money supply and currency; fiscal concerns taxing and spending by the government.
entries.definitionCN: 指货币供应与通货；fiscal 关乎政府的征税与支出。

entries.definition: Relating to a budget as a plan; fiscal can describe the whole year's accounts and the treasury behind them.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为计划的预算；fiscal 可以描述整年账目及其背后的国库。

entries.definition: Relating to money as a medium, often in legal writing about loss; it lacks the public-purse sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为媒介的金钱，常用于关于损失的法律文书；不含公家钱袋义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The basket is still inside the word: a woven chest where the state keeps its money.
normal.cn: 那只篮子仍在词里：国家存钱的编织箱。

normal.en: The family runs fisc, fiscal, fiscally, confiscate, confiscation, fiscal year.
normal.cn: 同族词包括国库、财政的、在财政上、没收、充公、财政年度。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the budget: fiscal year, fiscal deficit, fiscal discipline, fiscal stimulus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出预算的各个方面：财政年度、财政赤字、财政纪律、财政刺激。

normal.en: Confiscate is the same root used as a penalty: the property goes into the public chest.
normal.cn: 没收是同一词根用作处罚：财物被收进公家钱箱。

normal.en: In Scotland a fiscal is a prosecutor because the state's lawyer once acted for the treasury.
normal.cn: 在苏格兰，检察官也被叫作这个词，因为国家律师曾代国库行事。

abstract.en: Picture one chest with a tax bill going in at the top and a road coming out at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱箱，上面进税单，下面出一条公路。

abstract.en: Picture a household calendar whose year ends in March, not December.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历，年份在三月底而非十二月底结束。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp in the corner of a deed, small but able to stop a sale.
abstract.cn: 想象契据角上的一枚印花，虽小却能拦住一笔买卖。

examples.en: The fiscal cost of the war outlasted the fighting by a generation.
examples.cn: 这场战争的财政代价在战事结束后还延续了一代人。

examples.en: Fiscal rules were tightened after the deficit exceeded the legal limit.
examples.cn: 赤字超过法定上限后，财政规则被收紧。

examples.en: The fiscal year ends in June, so the accounts close before the summer recess.
examples.cn: 财政年度在六月结束，账目在夏季休会前结清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「钱筐」——公家把钱装进筐里，进的是税、出的是公共开支 → 财政的

root: 拉丁 fiscus 原指编织篮，后指罗马国库的钱箱，再指国库机构；形容词 fiscalis「国库的」经古法语 fiscal 于 16 世纪入英语。同根词有 confiscate、confiscation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one chest: what goes into it, the year it is counted over, the balance left at the end, the discipline of not overdrawing it, extra spending in a slump, the weight on those who fill it, the stamp that proves a tax was paid, and the lawyer who once spoke for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一只钱箱：装进去的东西、按什么年度结账、年终剩下的差额、不透支的纪律、衰退时的额外支出、向填箱者施加的重量、证明缴税的印花，以及曾替它说话的律师。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a public chest with a tax bill entering at the top and a public work leaving at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只公家钱箱，上面进税单，下面出公共工程。

branches.en: THE PURSE AND ITS WEIGHT: what belongs to the chest, and what it costs those who fill it.
branches.cn: 钱袋与重量：属于钱箱的东西，以及填箱者为此付出的代价。

branches.en: THE COUNTING PERIOD: a chosen twelve months in which income and outgo are closed off.
branches.cn: 结算期间：被选定的十二个月，在此之内结清收入与支出。

branches.en: BALANCE AND DISCIPLINE: the difference at year end, and the rule against overdrawing it.
branches.cn: 差额与纪律：年终的差额，以及不得透支的规则。

branches.en: DELIBERATE EXPANSION: in a slump the chest is opened wider on purpose.
branches.cn: 有意扩张：衰退时故意把钱箱开得更大。

branches.en: PROOF AND ADVOCATE: the stamp proves the tax was paid, and the prosecutor once spoke for the chest.
branches.cn: 凭证与代言人：印花证明税已缴，检察官曾替钱箱说话。

intro.en: Fiscal is a Latin adjective from the word for the public money chest; the root also gives the verb for taking property into that chest.
intro.cn: fiscal 是由「公家钱箱」一词派生的拉丁形容词；同一词根还给出「把财物收进钱箱」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fiscus and fiscalis stand behind fiscal, fisc and confiscate; the basket is the common image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fiscus 与 fiscalis 支撑 fiscal、fisc 与 confiscate；那只篮子是他们共同的意象。

items.example: The chest held the province's revenue.
items.exampleCN: 这只钱箱装着该省的税收。
该计划在财政上是中性的。

items.meaning: to take into the public chest
the act of taking into the chest

items.example: The fiscal year ends in March.

items.exampleCN: 改革后财政状况有所改善。
财政学者争论这条规则。

latinEntries.meaning: to lay up in the chest, confiscate

definition_zh: 财政政策（政府以税收与公共支出调节经济的措施）
definition_en: the government's use of taxation and public spending to influence the economy
core_image: 两只手在同一本账簿上动作，一只手加税，一只手拨款修路
scene: 经济连续两个季度收缩，财政部提出减税并加快修路，以财政政策托住需求。With output falling for two quarters, the treasury proposed tax cuts and faster road works as fiscal policy to support demand.
sceneCN: 这里指「政府用税收与支出来影响经济的措施」（第 1 个义项：以预算手段调节总需求）；句意为经济连续两个季度收缩，财政部提出减税并加快修路，以财政政策托住需求。可辨识物件：账簿、税单、修路图纸、公文包。

pos.zh: 财政政策（不可数）
作定语：财政政策的（如财政政策空间）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指各国各自的政策）

derivatives.zh: 短语的基础形容词，出自拉丁「国库的」→ 财政的
基础形容词加副词后缀 → 在财政上
短语的基础名词，经拉丁上溯希腊「城邦治理」→ 政策
基础名词加表示制定者的复合成分 → 决策者
前缀义为「收拢」加钱箱词根，再加动词后缀 → 没收

senses.title: The government's budget stance overall
senses.titleCN: 政府预算的总立场
senses.definition: the general direction set by a government through its taxing and spending decisions
senses.definitionCN: 政府通过征税与支出决定所定的总方向
senses.example: Fiscal policy was neutral for most of the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这十年里的大部分时间，财政政策是中性的。
senses.why: fiscal points at the public purse and policy at a chosen course, so the phrase is the course a government chooses for its budget.
senses.whyCN: 「财政的」指向公家钱袋，「政策」指向选定的路线，合起来就是政府为预算选定的路线。

senses.title: Expansionary policy through spending or tax cuts
senses.titleCN: 以增支或减税实现的扩张性政策
senses.definition: a deliberate widening of the deficit to raise demand and employment
senses.definitionCN: 有意扩大赤字以提高需求与就业
senses.example: Expansionary fiscal policy shortened the downturn but left a larger debt.
senses.exampleCN: 扩张性财政政策缩短了低迷期，却留下更大的债务。
senses.why: if the private sector stops spending, the government can spend in its place, which is why the deficit is widened on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 如果私人部门停止支出，政府可以替它支出，因此赤字被有意扩大。

senses.title: Contractionary policy or austerity
senses.titleCN: 紧缩性政策或财政紧缩
senses.definition: a deliberate narrowing of the deficit through higher taxes or lower spending
senses.definitionCN: 通过加税或减支有意缩小赤字
senses.example: Contractionary fiscal policy was imposed as a condition of the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 紧缩性财政政策作为贷款条件被强制实施。
senses.why: the mirror image of expansion: when debt is judged too high, the chest is closed rather than opened.
senses.whyCN: 这是扩张的镜像：当债务被认为过高时，钱箱被关上而不是打开。

senses.title: Automatic stabilizers built into the budget
senses.titleCN: 预算中自带的自动稳定器
senses.definition: features such as unemployment benefits that expand or shrink without a new law
senses.definitionCN: 失业救济之类无需新立法即自动扩张或收缩的安排
senses.example: Automatic stabilizers did much of the work before any fiscal policy was voted on.
senses.exampleCN: 在任何财政政策付诸表决之前，自动稳定器已经起了大部分作用。
senses.why: some spending follows the cycle by design, so the budget stabilizes demand even when no one acts, and this is counted as part of the policy.
senses.whyCN: 有些支出按设计随周期起落，即使无人行动预算也在稳定需求，这部分也算作政策。

senses.title: Discretionary measures voted in a downturn
senses.titleCN: 衰退中经表决的相机抉择措施
senses.definition: one-off decisions such as a stimulus package or a temporary tax holiday
senses.definitionCN: 一次性决定，如刺激方案或临时减税期
senses.example: The discretionary part of fiscal policy was small compared with the automatic part.
senses.exampleCN: 财政政策中相机抉择的部分比起自动部分要小。
senses.why: the part that needs a vote is only the tip; most of the budget moves with the cycle on its own.
senses.whyCN: 需要表决的只是尖端，大部分预算随周期自行起落。

senses.title: Fiscal consolidation to restore the balance
senses.titleCN: 以财政整顿恢复收支平衡
senses.definition: a planned combination of tax rises and spending cuts to bring debt under control
senses.definitionCN: 为控制债务而计划实施的加税与减支组合
senses.example: Fiscal consolidation was delayed until recovery was secure.
senses.exampleCN: 财政整顿被推迟到复苏稳固之后。
senses.why: repair is not a single act but a programme stretched over years, which is why it has its own name.
senses.whyCN: 修补不是单一动作，而是拉长数年的方案，因此有自己的名字。

senses.title: A stimulus package as a single act
senses.titleCN: 作为单独立法的刺激方案
senses.definition: a named law or programme that spends or cuts taxes within a fixed period
senses.definitionCN: 在固定期限内支出或减税的具名法律或计划
senses.example: The stimulus package was the largest fiscal policy action since the war.
senses.exampleCN: 该刺激方案是战后最大的财政政策行动。
senses.why: a package bundles many measures under one vote, so the whole bundle is spoken of as one action.
senses.whyCN: 方案把许多措施捆在一次表决之下，整捆便被当作一个动作来说。

senses.title: Coordination with monetary policy
senses.titleCN: 与货币政策的配合
senses.definition: the setting of the budget in view of what the central bank is doing with rates
senses.definitionCN: 参照央行利率动作来设定预算
senses.example: Fiscal policy and monetary policy pulled in opposite directions for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 有一年，财政政策与货币政策朝相反方向用力。
senses.why: the two authorities act on the same demand, so their settings are always read against each other.
senses.whyCN: 两个当局作用于同一需求，因此彼此的设定总被相互对照。

intro.en: The phrase joins fiscal, from Latin fiscus 'money chest', with policy, from Greek politeia 'government' by way of Latin and French. It became standard in the twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把来自拉丁 fiscus「钱箱」的 fiscal 与经拉丁语、法语上溯希腊 politeia「治理」的 policy 连在一起，20 世纪成为标准术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fiscus moved from a woven basket to the chest of the Roman treasury and then to the treasury as an institution.
items.cn: fiscus 从编织篮转为罗马国库的钱箱，再转为作为机构的国库。

items.en: Fiscalis meant 'of the treasury', and Old French fiscal brought it into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: fiscalis 意为「国库的」，古法语 fiscal 于 16 世纪把它带入英语。

items.en: Politeia named citizenship and the running of a city; Latin politia and Old French policie carried it toward English policy.
items.cn: politeia 指公民身份与城邦治理；拉丁 politia 与古法语 policie 把它带向英语 policy。

items.en: Policy first meant a system of government, and only later any deliberate course of action chosen by an authority.
items.cn: policy 先指治理体系，后来才指权威选定的任何有意路线。

items.en: Fiscal policy became a standard term in the 1930s and 1940s, when governments took explicit responsibility for managing demand.
items.cn: 财政政策在 20 世纪 30 与 40 年代成为标准术语，当时政府明确承担管理总需求的职责。

items.en: Automatic stabilizers, consolidation and fiscal space were added as named parts of the same practice in the later twentieth century.
items.cn: 自动稳定器、财政整顿与财政空间在 20 世纪后期作为同一实践的有名部分被添入。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the chest or on government; group two holds policies and measures that are often compared with it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「钱箱」或「治理」词根的词；第二组是常与之比较的政策与措施。

entries.definition: Relating to public money; the full phrase adds that a deliberate course is being followed.
entries.definitionCN: 指与公款有关；整个短语另含「正在遵循一条有意路线」。

entries.definition: In public-money terms; it describes how an action is done, not which policy it is.
entries.definitionCN: 指从公款角度；它描述动作方式，而非政策本身。

entries.definition: A settled course of action; alone it could concern health or trade rather than the budget.
entries.definitionCN: 指既定行动路线；单独使用时可以指卫生或贸易而非预算。

entries.definition: Of the body or of matter, from a Greek root; it shares only a sound with fiscal.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体或物质，出自希腊词根；与 fiscal 仅读音相近。

entries.definition: Central bank action through money and credit; fiscal policy acts through taxes and spending.
entries.definitionCN: 指央行通过货币与信贷行动；财政政策则通过税收与支出行动。

entries.definition: The annual plan of income and outgo; fiscal policy is the stance expressed through such plans.
entries.definitionCN: 指年度收支计划；财政政策是通过这类计划表达的立场。

entries.definition: Deliberate choices about who pays and how much; fiscal policy covers spending as well.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于谁缴、缴多少的有意选择；财政政策还包括支出。

entries.definition: A programme of cuts and tax rises to reduce debt; it is one setting of fiscal policy.
entries.definitionCN: 指以减支加税降低债务的方案；它只是财政政策的一种设定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The public chest plus a chosen course: how much goes in by tax and how much goes out by spending.
normal.cn: 公家钱箱加一条选定路线：收多少税进来，花多少钱出去。

normal.en: The family runs fiscal, fiscally, fisc, policy, policymaker, confiscate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括财政的、在财政上、国库、政策、政策制定者、没收。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: expansionary, contractionary, consolidation, fiscal space.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出设定：扩张性、紧缩性、整顿、财政空间。

normal.en: Automatic stabilizers work without a vote; discretionary measures need one.
normal.cn: 自动稳定器不经表决就起作用；相机抉择措施则需要表决。

normal.en: Two levers face each other: taxes and spending on one side, rates and money on the other.
normal.cn: 两根杠杆相对：一边是税收与支出，一边是利率与货币。

abstract.en: Picture one hand adding a tax line and another hand writing a road contract, on the same ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在账簿上加一行税，另一只手在同一本账簿上写公路合同。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat that warms the room when the outside turns cold, without anyone touching it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只恒温器，屋外变冷时它自己加热房间，无人触碰。

abstract.en: Picture a family that spends more in a hard year and must repay afterwards.
abstract.cn: 想象一户人家在艰难之年多花钱，之后必须补回来。

examples.en: Fiscal policy was the main tool left once interest rates reached zero.
examples.cn: 利率触零之后，财政政策成了剩下的主要工具。

examples.en: A credible fiscal policy can lower borrowing costs even before it is enacted.
examples.cn: 可信的财政政策甚至在立法之前就能降低借款成本。

examples.en: The two policies clashed: tight fiscal policy and easy monetary policy at the same time.
examples.cn: 两项政策相互冲突：财政政策紧缩的同时货币政策宽松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「财政的」加「政策」——政府一手加税、一手花钱，用这本账簿调节经济 → 财政政策

root: fiscal 来自拉丁 fiscus「钱箱、国库」及其形容词 fiscalis；policy 经拉丁 politia、古法语 policie 上溯希腊 politeia「公民身份、治理」，根为 polis「城邦」。复合术语在 20 世纪 30 至 40 年代定型。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses are one ledger held in different ways: the overall stance, the two directions of opening or closing the chest, the parts that move by themselves, the parts voted on, the repair of the balance, a single stimulus act, and the argument with the central bank.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一本账簿的八种拿法：总立场、开箱与关箱的两个方向、自己会动的部分、需要表决的部分、修补差额、单独立法的刺激行动，以及与央行的争论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands on one ledger, one adding a tax line, one writing a public works contract.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手在同一本账簿上，一只加税行，一只写公共工程合同。

branches.en: STANCE AND OPENING: the general course, and the deliberate widening of the deficit.
branches.cn: 立场与开箱：总路线，以及有意扩大赤字。

branches.en: CLOSING AND REPAIR: austerity closes the chest, consolidation plans the repair.
branches.cn: 关箱与修补：紧缩关上钱箱，整顿计划修补。

branches.en: SELF-MOVING PARTS: benefits and taxes that respond to the cycle without a new law.
branches.cn: 自己会动的部分：无需新立法即随周期反应的救济与税收。

branches.en: THE VOTED ACT: discretionary measures, and a named package as one large action.
branches.cn: 经表决的行动：相机抉择措施，以及作为单一大动作的具名方案。

branches.en: TWO LEVERS: the budget must be set with the central bank's rates in view.
branches.cn: 两根杠杆：设定预算时必须考虑央行的利率。

intro.en: The phrase is a Latin-derived adjective for the public chest plus a Greek-derived noun for a governing course.
intro.cn: 这个短语是一个表示公家钱箱的拉丁系形容词，加一个表示治理路线的希腊系名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fiscus and fiscalis supply the first half; Latin politia, from Greek politeia, supplies the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fiscus 与 fiscalis 提供前半；拉丁 politia（源自希腊 politeia）提供后半。

items.exampleCN: 这项措施在财政上是中性的。
政策制定者权衡了成本。

items.example: The polity is small but stable.
items.exampleCN: 这个政治共同体虽小却稳定。

definition_zh: 中央银行（负责发行货币、制定货币政策并维护金融稳定的国家级机构）
definition_en: the national institution that issues currency, sets monetary policy and safeguards the financial system
core_image: 一座没有营业柜台的大楼，地下金库堆着成袋现钞，楼顶装着一盏面向全国的信号灯
scene: 商业银行遭遇挤兑时，中央银行宣布提供紧急贷款，并保证存款人不会受损。When the commercial bank faced a run, the central bank offered emergency lending and assured depositors they would not lose their money.
sceneCN: 这里指「负责货币发行与金融稳定的国家级机构」（第 1 个义项：一国货币与银行体系的核心管理机构）；句意为商业银行遭遇挤兑时，中央银行提供紧急贷款，并向存款人作出保证。可辨识物件：石阶、金库门、信号灯、排队的人群。

pos.zh: 中央银行（可数，复数 central banks）
作定语：中央银行的（如央行独立性）

derivatives.zh: 与基础形容词同出希腊「圆规尖脚」的同源词 → 中心
短语的基础形容词，出自拉丁「中心的」→ 中心的
基础形容词加动词后缀，义为「使成为」→ 集中
短语的基础名词，出自意大利语「长凳」→ 银行
基础名词加表示人的后缀 → 银行家
基础名词加名词化后缀 → 银行业务

senses.title: The national monetary authority
senses.titleCN: 国家货币当局
senses.definition: the institution that manages a country's currency and credit at the highest level
senses.definitionCN: 在一国最高层面管理货币与信贷的机构
senses.example: The central bank published its annual report on monetary conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行发布了关于货币状况的年度报告。
senses.why: central marks the position at the middle of the system, and bank marks the money business, so the phrase is the bank at the centre of all the others.
senses.whyCN: 「中央的」标出它在体系中的位置，「银行」标出它的业务，合起来就是处在所有银行中心的那家银行。

senses.title: The issuer of notes and coin
senses.titleCN: 纸币与硬币的发行者
senses.definition: the body with the legal monopoly on issuing currency
senses.definitionCN: 拥有法定货币发行垄断权的机构
senses.example: Only the central bank may issue new notes.
senses.exampleCN: 只有中央银行可以发行新钞。
senses.why: a currency needs one issuer to be trusted, so the right to print was concentrated in a single national institution.
senses.whyCN: 货币需要一个发行者才可信，印钞权于是集中到一个国家级机构。

senses.title: The lender of last resort
senses.titleCN: 最后贷款人
senses.definition: the source of emergency funds when a solvent bank cannot borrow anywhere else
senses.definitionCN: 当有偿付能力的银行别处借不到钱时提供紧急资金的来源
senses.example: As lender of last resort, the central bank lent against good collateral.
senses.exampleCN: 作为最后贷款人，中央银行以优质抵押品为担保放贷。
senses.why: in a panic no private lender will step forward, so a public balance sheet must stand behind the system.
senses.whyCN: 恐慌时没有私人放贷者愿意出手，必须有一个公共资产负债表撑住体系。

senses.title: The setter of the policy rate
senses.titleCN: 政策利率的设定者
senses.definition: the body that decides the rate which anchors borrowing costs across the economy
senses.definitionCN: 决定锚定全经济借贷成本的那个利率的机构
senses.example: The central bank raised its policy rate by a quarter point.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行把政策利率提高了四分之一个百分点。
senses.why: one announced number is the clearest signal the institution sends, so the duty is often reduced to that number.
senses.whyCN: 一个被公布的号码是该机构发出的最清晰信号，因此这项职责常被简化为那个号码。

senses.title: The government's banker
senses.titleCN: 政府的银行
senses.definition: the institution that holds the state's accounts and manages its debt sales
senses.definitionCN: 持有国家账户并管理其债券发行的机构
senses.example: The treasury keeps its main account at the central bank.
senses.exampleCN: 财政部把主账户开在中央银行。
senses.why: the state also needs an account and a debt manager, and the central bank is the natural holder.
senses.whyCN: 国家也需要账户与债务管理者，中央银行是天然的保管者。

senses.title: The settlement centre for banks
senses.titleCN: 银行间的清算中心
senses.definition: the place where banks hold reserve accounts and settle payments with one another
senses.definitionCN: 各银行持有储备账户并相互结算支付的地方
senses.example: Payments between banks settle in accounts held at the central bank.
senses.exampleCN: 银行之间的支付在中央银行的账户中清算。
senses.why: banks must settle with each other daily, and only a common account keeper can do it safely.
senses.whyCN: 银行每天必须相互清算，只有共同的账户保管者才能安全完成。

senses.title: The supervisor of the banking system
senses.titleCN: 银行体系的监管者
senses.definition: the authority that licenses, examines and can close banks
senses.definitionCN: 负责发照、检查并可关闭银行的机构
senses.example: The central bank withdrew the licence after the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 审计之后，中央银行吊销了该行的执照。
senses.why: someone must decide which banks are sound, and that power sits with the body that can lend to them.
senses.whyCN: 必须有人判断哪些银行稳健，这项权力属于能向它们放贷的机构。

senses.title: An institution kept at arm's length from politics
senses.titleCN: 与政治保持距离的机构
senses.definition: the convention that day-to-day rate decisions are delegated rather than ordered by ministers
senses.definitionCN: 日常利率决定被授权而非由部长命令的惯例
senses.example: Central bank independence is meant to keep rate decisions out of election cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行的独立性意在让利率决定脱离选举周期。
senses.why: if ministers could set rates before elections, the temptation would be constant, so the duty is delegated.
senses.whyCN: 如果部长能在选举前定利率，诱惑将长期存在，因此这项职责被授权出去。

senses.title: A shared central bank for several states
senses.titleCN: 多国共用的中央银行
senses.definition: a supranational institution that acts as the monetary authority for a currency union
senses.definitionCN: 在货币联盟中充当货币当局的超国家机构
senses.example: The currency union gave its central bank one target and many members.
senses.exampleCN: 这个货币联盟给它的中央银行一个目标与许多成员。
senses.why: several states can share one currency only if they also share one issuer and one balance sheet.
senses.whyCN: 多国若要共用一种货币，就必须共用同一个发行者与同一张资产负债表。

intro.en: Central goes back through Latin centralis to Greek kentron 'sharp point, centre of a compass'; bank comes from Italian banca 'bench', the table of a money changer. The compound is a nineteenth-century formation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: central 经拉丁 centralis 上溯希腊 kentron「尖点、圆规的定针」；bank 来自意大利语 banca「长凳」，即钱币兑换商的桌子。这个复合词成形于 19 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kentron meant the point of a compass and the centre it fixes; Latin took it as centrum, the middle of anything.
items.cn: kentron 指圆规的尖脚及其定住的中心；拉丁语吸收为 centrum，指任何事物的中部。

items.en: Centralis 'of the centre' described the middle position, and English central entered through French in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: centralis「中心的」描述居中的位置，英语 central 于 17 世纪经法语进入。

items.en: A banca was a bench, and by extension the table where a money changer did business; the bench is the origin of the modern bank.
items.cn: banca 指长凳，引申指钱币兑换商做生意的桌子；这张长凳就是现代银行的来源。

items.en: English bank appeared in the fifteenth century for a money dealer's establishment, and the compound central bank followed in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 英语 bank 于 15 世纪指钱币商的营业处，复合词 central bank 则在 19 世纪跟上。

items.en: The Bank of England became the model of an institution that held the nation's reserves and lent in a crisis, and the label spread with it.
items.cn: 英格兰银行成为一个持有国家储备、在危机中放贷的机构范本，这一标签随之扩散。

items.en: In the twentieth century the same body took on policy rates, supervision and independence, and each of these became a distinct sense of the phrase.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，同一机构承担政策利率、监管与独立性，每一项都成为该短语的一个独立义项。

note.en: Group one holds words built on centre or on the bench; group two holds institutions and roles often confused with a central bank.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「中心」或「长凳」词根的词；第二组是常与中央银行混淆的机构与角色。

entries.definition: At the middle; the full phrase adds that the middle position belongs to a bank.
entries.definitionCN: 指居中的；整个短语另含「这个中间位置属于一家银行」。

entries.definition: The middle point itself; it says nothing about money or banking.
entries.definitionCN: 指中心点本身；与金钱或银行无关。

entries.definition: One who runs or works in a bank; a central bank is an institution, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指经营银行或在银行工作的人；中央银行是机构，不是个人。

entries.definition: The business of taking deposits and lending; a central bank sits above it rather than inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 指吸收存款与放贷的行业；中央银行位于其上方，而非其内部。

entries.definition: The government department that collects revenue and spends it; a central bank manages money and credit instead.
entries.definitionCN: 指负责征收与支出税款的政府部门；中央银行管理货币与信贷。

entries.definition: A bank that serves firms and households for profit; the central bank serves the system and not customers.
entries.definitionCN: 指为企业和家庭盈利性服务的银行；中央银行为体系而非客户服务。

entries.definition: A name used in some countries for the central bank, stressing its reserve-holding role.
entries.definitionCN: 一些国家对中央银行的称呼，强调其持有储备的职能。

entries.definition: A general term for the body that governs money; a central bank is its usual concrete form.
entries.definitionCN: 指管理货币的机构的一般称呼；中央银行是其常见的具体形态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Central is the compass point that holds the circle together; bank is the bench where money is handled.
normal.cn: 「中央」是让整个圆定住的圆规针脚，「银行」是处理钱的长凳。

normal.en: The family runs center, central, centralize, bank, banker, banking.
normal.cn: 同族词包括中心、中央的、集中、银行、银行家、银行业。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its duties: policy rate, reserves, independence, lender of last resort.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出职责：政策利率、储备、独立性、最后贷款人。

normal.en: The bench is still visible in bankrupt, which began as a broken bench.
normal.cn: 那张长凳仍看得见：破产一词本指被砸断的长凳。

normal.en: It is the bank that serves banks, not customers, which is why it has no ordinary counter.
normal.cn: 它是为银行服务的银行，不服务顾客，所以没有寻常柜台。

abstract.en: Picture a building with no teller windows, only a vault below and a signal lamp above.
abstract.cn: 想象一座没有出纳窗口的大楼，只有地下金库与楼顶信号灯。

abstract.en: Picture a row of smaller banks all keeping their accounts in one larger house.
abstract.cn: 想象一排小银行都把账户存在同一座大房子里。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a valve that every other bank watches before it moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手放在阀门上，其他银行都盯着它再行动。

examples.en: The central bank held rates steady while the government argued for cuts.
examples.cn: 央行维持利率不变，而政府主张降息。

examples.en: A central bank that loses credibility must work harder for the same effect.
examples.cn: 失去公信力的中央银行要为同样效果付出更多努力。

examples.en: The central bank's balance sheet expanded sharply during the crisis.
examples.cn: 危机期间，中央银行的资产负债表急剧扩张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「中央」加「银行」——站在所有银行正中间的那一家，管发钞、管利率、危机时兜底 → 中央银行

root: central 经拉丁 centralis 上溯希腊 kentron「尖点、圆规定针」；bank 来自意大利语 banca「长凳」，即钱币兑换商的桌子，破产一词本指断凳。复合词成形于 19 世纪，以英格兰银行为范本。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all belong to one institution seen from nine duties: the top authority, the issuer, the emergency lender, the rate setter, the state's banker, the clearing house, the supervisor, the independent body and the shared bank of a currency union.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都属于同一机构，从九项职责看它：最高当局、发行者、紧急放贷者、利率设定者、政府的银行、清算所、监管者、独立机构，以及货币联盟共用的银行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one house at the centre of a circle of banks, holding the vault and the signal lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈银行正中的一座房子，内有金库，顶有信号灯。

chain: IT LENDS WHEN ALL OTHERS STOP
IT WATCHES AND ANSWERS FOR ALL

branches.en: AUTHORITY AND ORIGIN: the top body is also the only lawful source of new notes.
branches.cn: 权威与源头：最高机构同时也是新钞的唯一合法来源。

branches.en: WHEN THE SYSTEM STOPS: emergency lending keeps a solvent bank alive, and the policy rate sets the price of credit.
branches.cn: 体系停摆时：紧急放贷让有偿付能力的银行存活，政策利率定下信贷价格。

branches.en: THE STATE AND THE CLEARING HOUSE: it keeps the government's account and settles payments among banks.
branches.cn: 国家与清算所：它保管政府账户，并在银行之间清算支付。

branches.en: THE WATCHER: it licenses, examines and can close a bank.
branches.cn: 看守者：它发照、检查，并可关闭一家银行。

branches.en: DISTANCE FROM POLITICS: independence protects decisions from election cycles, and a shared bank serves many states at once.
branches.cn: 与政治的距离：独立性让决定脱离选举周期，共用银行则同时服务多国。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived word for the middle with an Italian word for a money changer's bench; both halves brought families into English.
intro.cn: 这个短语把源自希腊语、表示「中部」的词，与源自意大利语、表示「钱币商长凳」的词连在一起；两半都给英语带来词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek kentron became Latin centrum and centralis; Italian banca became Medieval Latin bancus and English bank.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 kentron 变成拉丁 centrum 与 centralis；意大利 banca 变成中世纪拉丁 bancus 与英语 bank。

items.example: The stone marks the center of the square.
items.exampleCN: 这块石头标出广场的中心。

items.meaning: the act of bringing to one point
items.exampleCN: 集中化拖慢了地方决策。
这位银行家拒绝了贷款。

items.meaning: a promise to pay issued by a bank
items.example: The note bears the bank's name.
items.exampleCN: 这张纸币印着银行的名字。

bancus, -i (m., Medieval Latin, from Italian banca)

definition_zh: 保留；储备；预订；后备人员；保护区；克制寡言
definition_en: to keep or set aside for future use; a store kept back, a force or place held for emergencies, or restraint in manner
core_image: 一只贴着封条的柜子，里面整齐码着暂不动用的物资，钥匙挂在值班室墙上
scene: 雨季结束时，水库管理员把多余的水留在库中备用，只放出河流需要的最小流量。At the end of the wet season the reservoir keeper held the surplus in reserve and released only the minimum flow the river needed.
sceneCN: 这里指「留待以后动用的储备」（第 2 个义项：被保存下来、暂不使用的那一部分）；句意为雨季结束时，水库管理员把多余的水留作储备，只放出河流所需的最小流量。可辨识物件：封条柜、水尺、闸门、钥匙。

pos.zh: 保留；预留；推迟（判断、权利等）
储备（物）；后备队；保护区；预订；克制

基础动词加名词后缀 → 预订；保留

senses.title: To set something aside for later
senses.titleCN: 把某物留到以后再用
senses.definition: to keep something unused now so that it is available when needed
senses.definitionCN: 现在不使用某物，以便需要时可用
senses.example: We reserve two seats for late arrivals.
senses.exampleCN: 我们为迟到者留了两个座位。
senses.why: the verb is built from a prefix meaning back and a verb meaning keep, so its core is to keep something back from present use.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词由表示「向后」的前缀与表示「守住」的动词构成，核心是把某物从当下用途中留出来。

senses.title: A store kept back
senses.titleCN: 被留下的储备
senses.definition: a supply of something held unused against a future need
senses.definitionCN: 为将来需要而留存、尚未动用的供应
senses.example: The granary holds a year's reserve of wheat.
senses.exampleCN: 这座粮仓存着够一年用的小麦储备。
senses.why: the noun is the object produced by the act: whatever has been kept back becomes the reserve.
senses.whyCN: 名词是动作留下的东西：凡被留出的，就成了储备。

senses.title: Military forces held back from the front
senses.titleCN: 不投入前线、留待调用的部队
senses.definition: soldiers or equipment kept out of the first line so they can be sent where needed
senses.definitionCN: 不放在第一线、以便随时调往需要处的兵员或装备
senses.example: The general kept two brigades in reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 将军把两个旅留作预备队。
senses.why: a commander cannot commit everything at once, so part of the force is deliberately kept out of the first line.
senses.whyCN: 指挥官不能一次投入全部力量，因此有意把一部分兵力留在第一线之外。

senses.title: A protected area for nature
senses.titleCN: 为自然保留的保护区域
senses.definition: land set aside where wildlife and habitat are protected from development
senses.definitionCN: 为保护野生生物与生境、禁止开发而留出的土地
senses.example: The marsh was declared a nature reserve in 1978.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沼泽在 1978 年被宣布为自然保护区。
senses.why: land is set apart by law so that one use is excluded, and exclusion is the same idea as reserving.
senses.whyCN: 土地依法律被划出，使某类用途被排除，而「排除」与「保留」是同一观念。

senses.title: A substitute player
senses.titleCN: 替补球员
senses.definition: an athlete kept ready to replace one who is injured or out of form
senses.definitionCN: 随时准备替换受伤或状态不佳者的运动员
senses.example: The reserve goalkeeper warmed up alone.
senses.exampleCN: 替补门将独自热身。
senses.why: a team needs a ready replacement, so one place in the squad is kept for a player not yet used.
senses.whyCN: 球队需要随时可用的替代者，因此队中留出一个位置给尚未出场的球员。

senses.title: Money held for emergencies
senses.titleCN: 为应急留存的资金
senses.definition: funds kept by a bank, firm or state to meet unexpected demands
senses.definitionCN: 银行、企业或国家为应对意外需求而留存的资金
senses.example: The bank's reserves fell below the required level.
senses.exampleCN: 该行的储备降到了规定水平之下。
senses.why: payments can arrive before income does, so a stock of cash must be kept against the gap.
senses.whyCN: 付款可能先于收入到来，因此必须留出一笔现金应对缺口。

senses.title: An advance booking
senses.titleCN: 提前订下的位置
senses.definition: an arrangement that keeps a seat, room or table for a named person
senses.definitionCN: 为特定的人保留座位、房间或餐桌的安排
senses.example: She made a reservation for four at seven.
senses.exampleCN: 她订了七点四个人的位子。
senses.why: booking is an act of keeping something back from others, so the same idea appears as a noun in the catering trade.
senses.whyCN: 预订是把某物从他人手中留出的动作，同一观念于是以名词形式出现在餐饮业。

senses.title: The minimum price at an auction
senses.titleCN: 拍卖中的最低成交价
senses.definition: the lowest figure a seller will accept before an item is withdrawn
senses.definitionCN: 卖方在撤下拍品之前愿意接受的最低数字
senses.example: The painting failed to reach its reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画没有达到保留价。
senses.why: the seller sets a floor below which the item is withheld, which is the act of reserving applied to a price.
senses.whyCN: 卖方设定一个下限，低于此价便撤回拍品，这正是「保留」动作用在价格上。

senses.title: Restraint or aloofness in manner
senses.titleCN: 举止上的克制与疏离
senses.definition: the habit of not showing feelings or opinions freely
senses.definitionCN: 不轻易表露感情或意见的习惯
senses.example: His reserve made the new staff uneasy.
senses.exampleCN: 他的矜持让新员工感到不自在。
senses.why: a person who keeps something back in speech behaves like a store kept back from use, so the noun shifted from goods to manner.
senses.whyCN: 在言语上把东西留住的人，其行为就像被留出的储备，名词于是从货物转到举止。

senses.title: A tract set aside for a community
senses.titleCN: 为特定社群留出的地域
senses.definition: land reserved by treaty or law for a particular people, as in North America
senses.definitionCN: 依条约或法律为特定族群留出的土地，如北美情形
senses.example: The river forms the northern edge of the reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河构成该保留地的北界。
senses.why: the same act of setting land apart produced a third institutional sense: the reserved tract has its own government and boundaries.
senses.whyCN: 同样是「把土地划出」的动作，产出了第三个制度义：被保留的地域有自己的治理与边界。

intro.en: Reserve comes from Latin reservare 'to keep back', built on re- 'back' and servare 'to keep, guard'. It reached English through Old French in the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: reserve 来自拉丁 reservare「留住、留下」，由 re-「向后」与 servare「守住、看护」构成，14 世纪经古法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Servare meant 'to keep, guard, preserve'. A link to servus 'slave' is often mentioned but is not settled, and the deeper origin is treated as reconstructed.
items.cn: servare 意为「守住、看护、保存」。人们常提到它与 servus「奴隶」的联系，但并无定论，更深来源按重构处理。

items.en: Re- 'back' plus servare gave reservare, 'to keep back, to hold in store, to except'. The prefix is what makes the keeping deliberate rather than mere guarding.
items.cn: re-「向后」加 servare 构成 reservare，意为「留回、存下、除外」。前缀才使这种保存成为有意的留存，而不只是看护。

items.en: Old French reserver passed the verb to English in the fourteenth century, first in legal language about rights kept back.
items.cn: 古法语 reserver 于 14 世纪把这个动词传给英语，最初见于关于保留权利的法律语言。

items.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the noun extended to troops kept from the front and to money kept against emergencies.
items.cn: 在 17 与 18 世纪，名词扩展到不投入前线的部队，以及为应急留存的资金。

items.en: The nineteenth century added the reserved tract of land and the advance booking of a seat, both being things kept for a named purpose.
items.cn: 19 世纪添上被留出的土地与座位的预订，二者都是为特定用途留下的东西。

items.en: The sense of personal restraint is recorded later and rests on a metaphor: feelings, like goods, are kept in store rather than shown.
items.cn: 个人克制的义项记录较晚，建立在隐喻之上：感情像货物一样被存起来而不摆出来。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the keeping root or close in shape; group two holds near neighbours that name other kinds of stored supply.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「保存」词根或形近的词；第二组是表示其他种类留存供应的近义词。

entries.definition: Kept for someone, or restraint in manner; it describes a state rather than the stock itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某人留出，或举止矜持；它描述状态而非储备物本身。

entries.definition: A booking, a tract of land, or a doubt kept back; the noun covers the results of reserving.
entries.definitionCN: 指预订、保留地或保留意见；这个名词涵盖保留动作的各种结果。

entries.definition: A lake or tank that stores water; it is the place where a reserve of water is held.
entries.definitionCN: 指蓄水的湖或池；它是水的储备被存放之处。

entries.definition: To keep something safe from harm or decay; the prefix means before, and the focus is protection rather than storage.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物免于损害或腐坏；前缀意为「先」，重点在保护而非储藏。

entries.definition: A big accumulated store, often of weapons or fuel; reserve is the more general word for what is kept back.
entries.definitionCN: 指大量堆积的储存，常指武器或燃料；reserve 是更一般的「留出」说法。

entries.definition: A person or copy ready to replace the original; it stresses replacement rather than storage.
entries.definitionCN: 指准备替代原件的备份或替补；强调替代而非储存。

entries.definition: The quantity on hand for current use; a reserve is specifically the part not meant for current use.
entries.definitionCN: 指当下可用的数量；储备专指不供当下使用的部分。

entries.definition: Holding back an impulse or feeling; it covers the personal sense of reserve but not the stores.
entries.definitionCN: 指抑制冲动或情感；只覆盖 reserve 的个人义，不指储备物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The core is keep back: a prefix meaning back joined to a verb meaning guard.
normal.cn: 核心是「留住」：表示「向后」的前缀加上表示「守住」的动词。

normal.en: The family runs reserve, reserved, reservation, reservoir, preserve, conservation, observatory.
normal.cn: 同族词包括保留、矜持的、预订、水库、保存、保护、观测站。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the kinds: in reserve, nature reserve, reserve price, foreign exchange reserves.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类型：留作备用、自然保护区、保留价、外汇储备。

normal.en: A reservation is something kept back from other people, whether a table or a doubt.
normal.cn: 预订就是把某物从他人那里留出，无论是一张桌子还是一条保留意见。

normal.en: The same verb guards a nature reserve, an army reserve and a bank's reserves.
normal.cn: 同一个动词守着自然保护区、军队预备队与银行储备。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed cupboard of supplies with the key hanging in the duty room.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封好的物资柜，钥匙挂在值班室墙上。

abstract.en: Picture a goalkeeper on the bench, gloves already on.
abstract.cn: 想象替补门将坐在长椅上，手套已经戴好。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet guest who says little and keeps his opinions in a locked drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一位沉默的客人，话很少，把意见锁在抽屉里。

examples.en: The state kept a month's fuel in reserve against a sudden cutoff.
examples.cn: 国家留着一个月的燃料储备，以防突然断供。

examples.en: She reserved her judgement until the second report arrived.
examples.cn: 她保留判断，直到第二份报告到手。

examples.en: The reserve price was set high enough to protect the seller.
examples.cn: 保留价定得足够高，以保护卖方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向后」的前缀加「守住」的词根——把东西守回来、留下来不动，就是储备；把话也留住不说，就是矜持

root: 拉丁 reservare「留住」= re-「向后」+ servare「守住、看护」，经古法语 reserver 于 14 世纪入英语；同根词有 preserve、conservation、observatory。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses all come from one act: keeping something back. What is kept can be goods, troops, land, money, a seat, a minimum price, a judgement, a feeling or a whole tract for a community.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项都出自同一个动作：把东西留住。被留住的可以是货物、部队、土地、金钱、座位、底价、判断、情感，或一整片给特定社群的地域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed cupboard of supplies whose key hangs in the duty room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只封好的物资柜，钥匙挂在值班室墙上。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE STOCK: one verb keeps things back, and the thing kept becomes the noun.
branches.cn: 动作与存量：动词把东西留住，被留住的就成名词。

branches.en: PEOPLE HELD READY: soldiers and substitute players wait outside the first line.
branches.cn: 留待调用的人：士兵与替补球员在第一线之外等待。

branches.en: LAND SET APART: nature is protected in one tract, a community is given another.
branches.cn: 划出的土地：一处用于保护自然，另一处给予特定社群。

branches.en: MONEY AND PRICE: funds wait for a run, and a minimum price guards a seller.
branches.cn: 金钱与价格：资金等着挤兑，最低价守着卖方。

branches.en: WHAT IS WITHHELD: a table held for a guest, and a feeling held out of sight.
branches.cn: 被留住的东西：为客人留的桌位，以及藏起来的感情。

intro.en: Reserve is a Latin verb of prefix plus root, and the root for guarding also builds preserve, conservation and observatory.
intro.cn: reserve 是前缀加词根的拉丁动词，表示「看护」的词根还构成 preserve、conservation 与 observatory。

latinIntro.en: Latin servare 'to keep' yields reservare, preservare and conservare, and English taken all three.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 servare「守住」衍生出 reservare、preservare 与 conservare，英语把三者都吸收了。

items.example: The clerk served the next customer.
items.exampleCN: 职员接待了下一位顾客。

items.example: They reserve a room for him.
items.exampleCN: 他们为他留了一个房间。

items.meaning: a place where water is stored
items.example: The reservoir is low this year.
Preservation of the site cost millions.

items.exampleCN: 保护团体反对这条公路。

items.example: The observatory sits on the ridge.

definition_zh: 流动性；变现能力；流动资金状况；（市场的）成交深度
definition_en: the ease with which an asset can be turned into cash without losing value, or the cash and near-cash a firm or market holds
core_image: 一排货架，最左边的东西一伸手就能换成钱，越往右越难卖出
scene: 危机爆发时，银行发现账面资产很多，能立刻换成现金的却极少，流动性骤然紧张。When the crisis hit, the bank found it held plenty of assets but few it could turn into cash at once, and liquidity tightened sharply.
sceneCN: 这里指「资产迅速变现的能力」（第 1 个义项：在不显著损失价值的前提下换成现金的容易程度）；句意为危机爆发时，银行发现账面资产很多，能立刻换成现金的却极少，流动性骤然紧张。可辨识物件：货架、价签、现金抽屉、风险曲线。

pos.zh: 流动性；变现能力（不可数；复数形式少用）

forms.label: 复数（少用，指多种流动性指标）

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「流动的」→ 液体的；易变现的
基础形容词加动词后缀 → 变现；清算
由该动词加名词后缀 → 清算；破产变卖
基础词干加使动后缀 → 使液化
否定前缀加基础形容词 → 不易变现的

senses.title: Ease of turning an asset into cash
senses.titleCN: 资产换成现金的容易程度
senses.definition: the speed and certainty with which an asset can be sold for cash without a price concession
senses.definitionCN: 资产能在不折价的情况下换成现金的速度与确定性
senses.example: Government bonds offer high liquidity because a buyer is always near.
senses.exampleCN: 政府债券流动性高，因为买家总在附近。
senses.why: the word is the noun of being liquid: what flows can change shape at once, and an asset that flows into cash does the same.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「呈液态」的名词：能流动之物可立刻改变形状，能流成现金的资产亦然。

senses.title: Cash and near-cash held by a firm
senses.titleCN: 企业持有的现金与准现金
senses.definition: the money and easily sold instruments available to meet payments as they fall due
senses.definitionCN: 在到期付款时能动用的现金与易于出售的票据
senses.example: The company kept enough liquidity to cover three months of wages.
senses.exampleCN: 公司留住了足够支付三个月工资的流动性。
senses.why: wages and suppliers must be paid on fixed dates, so a buffer of spendable money is held against them.
senses.whyCN: 工资与供货商须在固定日期付款，因此要留一笔可随时支用的钱应对。

senses.title: Depth in a trading market
senses.titleCN: 交易市场的深度
senses.definition: the condition in which large trades can be made quickly without moving the price much
senses.definitionCN: 大额交易能迅速完成而价格变动不大的状态
senses.example: Liquidity in the small-cap market vanished after the rule change.
senses.exampleCN: 规则变更后，小盘股市场的流动性消失了。
senses.why: a market can only absorb size if enough orders rest on both sides, so depth is measured as liquidity.
senses.whyCN: 市场只有在买卖两侧挂着足够订单时才能吸收大额交易，因此深度以流动性来衡量。

senses.title: Bank liquidity under regulation
senses.titleCN: 监管意义上的银行流动性
senses.definition: the stock of liquid assets a bank must hold against a run, measured by agreed ratios
senses.definitionCN: 银行必须持有以应对挤兑的流动资产存量，按约定比率衡量
senses.example: The new rules raised the liquidity every bank had to keep.
senses.exampleCN: 新规则提高了每家银行必须保持的流动性。
senses.why: a run can drain a bank in days, so regulators require a stock of assets that can be sold at once.
senses.whyCN: 挤兑能在几天内抽干一家银行，监管者因此要求持有一批可立刻出售的资产。

senses.title: Funding liquidity, or access to borrowing
senses.titleCN: 融资流动性，即借入资金的能力
senses.definition: the ability to raise cash in the market rather than by selling assets
senses.definitionCN: 在市场筹得现金、而非靠卖资产的能力
senses.example: Funding liquidity dried up first, before asset prices fell.
senses.exampleCN: 融资流动性先枯竭，资产价格随后才下跌。
senses.why: cash can come from selling or from borrowing, and the borrowing route is a separate kind of liquidity.
senses.whyCN: 现金可以来自卖资产，也可以来自借钱，而借钱这条路是另一类流动性。

senses.title: A liquidity crunch or crisis
senses.titleCN: 流动性紧缩或危机
senses.definition: a short period in which cash is hard to obtain and normal payments seize up
senses.definitionCN: 现金难以取得、正常支付骤停的短时期
senses.example: The liquidity crunch forced sound firms to borrow at punitive rates.
senses.exampleCN: 流动性紧缩迫使稳健企业以惩罚性利率借款。
senses.why: when everyone wants cash at once, the flow reverses and the shortage becomes a named event.
senses.whyCN: 当所有人都同时要现金时，流向逆转，短缺就变成一个有名字的事件。

senses.title: Liquidity preference in economics
senses.titleCN: 经济学中的流动性偏好
senses.definition: the desire to hold money rather than other assets because money can be spent at once
senses.definitionCN: 因货币可随时花用而宁愿持有货币、不持有其他资产的愿望
senses.example: Liquidity preference rises when people fear a fall in bond prices.
senses.exampleCN: 当人们担心债券价格下跌时，流动性偏好上升。
senses.why: money is the one asset that needs no sale, so a fear of falling prices makes people prefer it.
senses.whyCN: 货币是唯一无需出售的资产，对价格下跌的恐惧因此让人更愿意持有它。

senses.title: The physical state of flowing
senses.titleCN: 物质呈流动状态的属性
senses.definition: the property of a substance that flows, a rare and largely literal use
senses.definitionCN: 物质可流动的属性，属少见而接近字面的用法
senses.example: The experiment measured the liquidity of the heated wax.
senses.exampleCN: 实验测量了加热后蜡的流动性。
senses.why: the financial senses all rest on the literal property, which still appears in laboratory and technical use.
senses.whyCN: 所有金融义都建立在字面的物理属性上，后者仍出现在实验室与技术用法中。

intro.en: Liquidity is the noun of Latin liquidus 'fluid, clear', from liquere 'to be fluid'. English built it with the noun suffix -ity in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: liquidity 是拉丁 liquidus「流动的、清澈的」的名词形式，其动词为 liquere「呈液态」。英语在 17 世纪以名词后缀 -ity 构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Liquere meant 'to be fluid, to flow, to be clear'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and the usual Indo-European reconstruction is not a demonstrated fact.
items.cn: liquere 意为「呈液态、流动、清澈」。其更深来源不确定，常见的印欧语重构并非已证事实。

items.en: The adjective liquidus described water, oil and anything that flows, and also clear light or a plain style.
items.cn: 形容词 liquidus 描述水、油与一切流动之物，也用于清澈的光或平易的文风。

items.en: English liquid appears in the fourteenth century as both adjective and noun, first for flowing matter.
items.cn: 英语 liquid 于 14 世纪出现，既是形容词也是名词，最初指流动的物质。

items.en: The noun liquidity was formed on the adjective to name the quality of flowing, and early uses were largely physical.
items.cn: 名词 liquidity 在形容词上构成，用来命名「流动」这一性质，早期用法多为物理义。

items.en: In the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries political economy applied the word to assets that flow into cash, and to money available on demand.
items.cn: 在 19 与 20 世纪初，政治经济学把这个词用于能流成现金的资产，以及可随时动用的货币。

items.en: The later twentieth century added market depth and regulatory ratios, so one word now covers a firm, a market and a supervisor's test.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期又添上市场深度与监管比率，同一个词如今覆盖一家企业、一个市场与监管者的检验。

note.en: Group one holds words from the flowing root; group two holds near neighbours in finance that measure different things.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「流动」词根的词；第二组是金融中衡量其他指标的近义词。

entries.definition: Flowing, or easily sold; liquidity is the quality that the adjective names.
entries.definitionCN: 指流动的或易售出的；流动性正是这个形容词所命名的性质。

entries.tag: the verb of turning into cash
entries.definition: To sell assets or wind up a firm for cash; liquidity is the ease with which this can be done.
entries.definitionCN: 指出售资产或结束企业以取得现金；流动性是这件事的容易程度。

entries.definition: The winding up of a firm and sale of its assets; it may happen because liquidity was already gone.
entries.definitionCN: 指结束企业并变卖资产；它可能正因流动性已耗尽而发生。

entries.definition: Latin liquor meant fluid; English keeps it for a distilled drink, a very different path.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 liquor 意为流体；英语保留它指蒸馏酒，走向完全不同。

entries.definition: Whether assets exceed liabilities at all; a firm can be solvent and still lack liquidity.
entries.definitionCN: 指资产是否超过负债；一家企业可以有偿付能力却缺少流动性。

entries.definition: Whether an asset can find a buyer at all; liquidity adds that the sale is quick and does not move the price.
entries.definitionCN: 指资产能否找到买家；流动性另含「卖得快且不压价」。

entries.definition: The right to exchange one currency for another; liquidity concerns any asset turning into cash.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种货币兑换另一种的权利；流动性关乎任何资产变成现金。

entries.definition: The volume of orders resting in a market; it is a main support of market liquidity.
entries.definitionCN: 指市场中挂着的订单量；它是市场流动性的主要支撑。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The image is flow: what flows can become cash quickly, while what is frozen cannot.
normal.cn: 意象是流动：能流之物很快变成现金，冻住之物则不能。

normal.en: The family runs liquid, liquidity, liquidate, liquidation, liquefy, illiquid.
normal.cn: 同族词包括液体的、流动性、变现、清算、液化、不易变现的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the pressure: liquidity crunch, liquidity risk, liquidity ratio.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出压力：流动性紧缩、流动性风险、流动性比率。

normal.en: Solvency asks whether you owe more than you own; liquidity asks whether you can pay this week.
normal.cn: 偿付能力问你是否欠得比拥有的多；流动性问你这周拿不拿得出钱。

normal.en: Market liquidity is about finding a buyer fast without moving the price.
normal.cn: 市场流动性指快速找到买家而不推动价格。

abstract.en: Picture a row of goods on shelves, cash within reach at the left end and hard-to-sell items at the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一排货架上的货物，最左端伸手即可换钱，最右端是难卖的。

abstract.en: Picture ice melting into a cup, losing its shape but keeping its substance.
abstract.cn: 想象冰在杯中融成水，失去形状却保留实质。

abstract.en: Picture a crowded market where a buyer appears the moment a seller calls out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个拥挤的市场，卖方一喊就有买方出现。

examples.en: The fund held cash equal to a fifth of its assets, more liquidity than its rules required.
examples.cn: 该基金持有的现金相当于资产的两成，超过规则要求的流动性。

examples.en: Liquidity disappeared exactly when investors needed it most.
examples.cn: 流动性恰在投资者最需要它的时候消失了。

examples.en: A company can fail from a liquidity shortage while its balance sheet still looks sound.
examples.cn: 一家公司可能因流动性短缺而倒闭，账面却仍显得稳健。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「液体」的词根加名词后缀——能像水一样流成现金的东西，变现就越容易 → 流动性

root: 拉丁 liquidus「流动的、清澈的」来自 liquere「呈液态」；英语在 17 世纪加名词后缀构成 liquidity，19 世纪起用于金融，20 世纪后期扩展出市场深度与监管比率义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure flow: an asset into cash, a firm's cash, a market's depth, a bank's regulated stock, the ability to borrow, the moment the flow stops, the preference for cash, and the literal flowing of matter.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在衡量「流动」：资产流成现金、企业的现金、市场的深度、银行受监管的存量、借入的能力、流动停止的那一刻、对现金的偏好，以及物质字面上的流动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: goods on shelves, cash within reach at one end and frozen stock at the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：货架上的货物，一端伸手可换现金，另一端是冻住的存货。

branches.en: THE ASSET AND THE FIRM: how fast a holding becomes cash, and how much cash a firm keeps.
branches.cn: 资产与企业：持有物多快变成现金，以及企业留多少现金。

branches.en: TWO MARKETS: one is depth of trading, the other is access to borrowed cash.
branches.cn: 两种市场：一种是交易深度，另一种是借入现金的门路。

branches.en: THE REGULATOR'S TEST: a required stock of liquid assets measured by agreed ratios.
branches.cn: 监管者的检验：按约定比率衡量必须持有的流动资产。

branches.en: THE MOMENT IT STOPS: when cash cannot be had, normal payments seize up.
branches.cn: 停止的那一刻：现金取不到时，正常支付骤停。

branches.en: PREFERENCE AND PHYSICS: the wish to hold cash, and the literal flowing of a substance.
branches.cn: 偏好与物理：持有现金的愿望，以及物质字面上的流动。

intro.en: Liquidity is an adjective turned into a noun by a suffix; the root means to flow or to be clear.
intro.cn: liquidity 是形容词经后缀变成的名词，其词根意为「流动、清澈」。

latinIntro.en: Latin liquere and liquidus stand behind liquid, liquidity, liquefy and liquor; liquidation adds the sense of settling a debt.

senses.title: A substance that flows freely
senses.titleCN: 能自由流动的物质状态
senses.definition: matter with a definite volume but no fixed shape, which takes the shape of its container
senses.definitionCN: 有一定体积而无固定形状、随容器改变形状的物质
senses.example: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 汞是室温下唯一呈液态的金属。
senses.why: the adjective describes the state itself, and the noun names any substance in it, so the pair covers water, oil and melted metal.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述这一状态本身，名词指处于该状态的任何物质，因此水、油与熔化的金属都包括在内。

senses.title: Clear and translucent, as light or eyes
senses.titleCN: 清澈透亮的，如光或眼睛
senses.definition: describing something that lets light through and looks deep rather than cloudy
senses.definitionCN: 描述透光、显得深澈而不浑浊之物
senses.example: The lake was liquid green in the early sun.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨阳光下，湖面泛着清澈的绿。
senses.why: clear water was the original sight behind the word, and the quality was transferred to anything that seems to hold light within.
senses.whyCN: 清水是这个词背后的原始景象，这一性质随后被移到任何仿佛内含光亮之物上。

senses.title: Smooth and flowing in movement or sound
senses.titleCN: 动作或声音的流畅圆润
senses.definition: describing motion or music that runs without jerks, like a stream
senses.definitionCN: 描述动作或音乐毫无顿挫、如水般流淌
senses.example: Her liquid phrasing made the sonata seem easy.
senses.exampleCN: 她流畅的乐句让这首奏鸣曲显得轻松。
senses.why: what flows without obstruction is pleasant to watch or hear, so the physical idea became a word of praise for grace.
senses.whyCN: 无阻流动之物看着听着都舒服，物理观念于是变成赞美优雅的词。

senses.title: Easily turned into cash
senses.titleCN: 容易换成现金
senses.definition: describing an asset that can be sold quickly without a loss
senses.definitionCN: 描述能迅速售出而不损失价值的资产
senses.example: Treasury bills are the most liquid asset in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 短期国库券是市场上最容易变现的资产。
senses.why: cash itself flows, so an asset that becomes cash at once is described with the same word as water.
senses.whyCN: 现金本身会流动，能立刻变成现金的资产便与水共用同一个词。

senses.title: A market with many ready buyers
senses.titleCN: 买卖双方充足的市场
senses.definition: describing a market where large orders are absorbed without moving the price much
senses.definitionCN: 描述能吸收大额订单而价格变动不大的市场
senses.example: The shares became liquid only after the index inclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这些股票被纳入指数之后才变得易于成交。
senses.why: a market is liquid when orders wait on both sides, so a seller meets a buyer instead of waiting.
senses.whyCN: 市场两侧都挂着订单时才算易成交，卖方能直接遇到买方而不必等待。

senses.title: Cash and near-cash funds
senses.titleCN: 现金与准现金资金
senses.definition: describing money held in cash or in instruments that can be spent almost at once
senses.definitionCN: 描述以现金或几乎可即刻支用的票据持有的钱
senses.example: The firm kept half its wealth in liquid form.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业把一半财富以现金形式持有。
senses.why: wealth kept as cash can be spent without selling anything, which is the financial form of the same flow.
senses.whyCN: 以现金持有的财富无需出售任何东西就能支用，这是同一流动在金融上的形态。

senses.title: A liquid consonant in phonetics
senses.titleCN: 语音学中的流音
senses.definition: describing the sounds l and r, which flow into neighbouring sounds without friction
senses.definitionCN: 描述边音与颤音这类与相邻音平滑相接、不产生摩擦的音
senses.example: English has two liquid consonants in most analyses.
senses.exampleCN: 多数分析认为英语有两个流音。
senses.why: phonetics borrowed the flowing image because these sounds pass into their neighbours without a stop, unlike plosives.
senses.whyCN: 语音学借用「流动」意象，因为这些音与邻音相接而不阻塞，与爆破音不同。

senses.title: A liquid diet in medicine
senses.titleCN: 医学上的流质饮食
senses.definition: describing food taken as fluids for a period, often after surgery or during illness
senses.definitionCN: 描述在术后或病中一段时间内以流体形式进食
senses.example: He was on a liquid diet for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 他吃了三天流食。
senses.why: the medical use narrows the adjective to what can be swallowed as fluid, which is the oldest physical sense applied to care.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法把这个形容词收窄到可以以流质吞下的食物，这是最古老的物理义被用在照护上。

senses.title: Fluid, unsettled conditions in society
senses.titleCN: 社会中流动不定的状态
senses.definition: describing social or economic arrangements that change constantly and have no fixed form
senses.definitionCN: 描述不断变化、没有固定形态的社会或经济安排
senses.example: Bauman described modern life as liquid because nothing keeps its shape for long.
senses.exampleCN: 鲍曼把现代生活称作液态的，因为没有东西能长久保持形状。
senses.why: the metaphor extends flow from matter to institutions: what is liquid cannot be grasped and held, only followed.
senses.whyCN: 这一隐喻把流动从物质扩展到制度：液态之物抓不住、握不牢，只能跟随。

intro.en: Liquid comes from Latin liquidus 'fluid, clear', from liquere 'to be fluid'. English took it in the fourteenth century as both adjective and noun. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: liquid 来自拉丁 liquidus「流动的、清澈的」，其动词为 liquere「呈液态」。英语于 14 世纪把它同时吸收为形容词与名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Liquere meant 'to be fluid, to flow, to be clear'. Its earlier origin is uncertain, and the common reconstruction is a hypothesis rather than a proved form.
items.cn: liquere 意为「呈液态、流动、清澈」。其更早来源不确定，常见重构只是假说，并非已证形式。

items.en: Liquidus described water, oil and melted substances, and also clear light and a smooth style of speech.
items.cn: liquidus 描述水、油与熔化物，也用于清澈的光与平顺的言辞。

items.en: English liquid appears in the fourteenth century, at first for flowing matter; the noun and the adjective developed together.
items.cn: 英语 liquid 于 14 世纪出现，最初指流动的物质；名词与形容词同时发展。

items.en: Seventeenth-century grammars used liquid for sounds that flow into their neighbours, a technical borrowing of the water image.
items.cn: 17 世纪的语法学用 liquid 指流进邻音的音，这是对水的意象的技术性借用。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the adjective was applied to assets that turn into cash quickly, and liquid assets became a standard phrase.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，这个形容词被用于能迅速变成现金的资产，「流动资产」成为标准说法。

items.en: The twentieth and twenty-first centuries extended it to social arrangements that will not hold their shape, as in liquid modernity.
items.cn: 20 与 21 世纪把它扩展到无法保持形状的社会安排，如「液态现代性」。

note.en: Group one holds words from the flowing root or close in shape; group two holds adjectives that describe fluids, clarity or easy sale.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「流动」词根或形近的词；第二组是描述流体、清澈或易售的其他形容词。

entries.definition: The ease of turning assets into cash; liquid is the adjective that carries the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 指资产变现的容易程度；liquid 是承载同一观念的形容词。

entries.definition: A distilled alcoholic drink, from Latin liquor 'fluid'; the modern sense is a narrow survival.
entries.definitionCN: 指蒸馏酒，来自拉丁 liquor「流体」；现代义是狭窄的存留。

entries.definition: To sell off assets or wind up a firm; it names the action that makes a holding liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 指出售资产或结束企业；它指使持有物变现的动作。

entries.definition: To make something fluid; it is about physical state, not money.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物液化；关乎物理状态，而非金钱。

entries.definition: A substance that flows; it is the everyday term, while liquid is the technical state between solid and gas.
entries.definitionCN: 指流动的物质；它是日常说法，liquid 是固气之间的技术状态。

entries.definition: Easy to see through; it covers the translucent sense but says nothing about flow or cash.
entries.definitionCN: 指容易看透；只覆盖清澈义，与流动或现金无关。

entries.definition: Free from bumps; it covers the flowing-motion sense but not the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有凹凸；覆盖流畅义，但不指物质状态。

entries.definition: Able to find a buyer; liquid adds that the sale is fast and does not move the price.
entries.definitionCN: 指能寻得买家；liquid 另含「卖得快且不压价」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Water is the original picture: it flows, it is clear, and it takes the shape of whatever holds it.
normal.cn: 水是原始图景：会流、清澈，并随容器改变形状。

normal.en: The family runs liquid, liquidity, liquefy, liquefaction, liquidate, liquor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括液体的、流动性、液化、液化过程、清算、蒸馏酒。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: liquid assets, liquid nitrogen, liquid crystal, liquid diet.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：流动资产、液氮、液晶、流食。

normal.en: In finance the test is simple: can it become cash this week without a discount?
normal.cn: 金融上的检验很简单：它这周能不能不折价地变成现金？

normal.en: In phonetics the same word names sounds that glide into their neighbours.
normal.cn: 在语音学中，同一个词指滑入邻音的那些音。

abstract.en: Picture water sliding down the inside of a glass while a coin at the bottom stays visible.
abstract.cn: 想象水沿杯壁滑下，杯底的硬币仍清晰可见。

abstract.en: Picture a stream that takes the shape of every stone it passes.
abstract.cn: 想象一条溪流，随经过的每块石头改变形状。

abstract.en: Picture a city where the buildings are replaced before anyone learns their names.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市，楼房在人们记住名字之前就被替换。

examples.en: The doctor put him on a liquid diet for two days after the operation.
examples.cn: 手术后医生让他吃了两天流食。

examples.en: Investors moved into liquid assets as the outlook darkened.
examples.cn: 前景转暗时，投资者转向流动资产。

examples.en: The market is liquid enough for a large order to be filled in minutes.
examples.cn: 这个市场的流动性足以让大额订单在几分钟内成交。

dict_mnemonic.text: 这个词听起来像「流克的」——能流的、清亮的；钱能立刻流成现金，就是易变现的

root: 拉丁 liquidus「流动的、清澈的」来自 liquere「呈液态」，更深来源不确定；英语 14 世纪吸收为形容词与名词，17 世纪进入语音学，19 世纪进入金融。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow flow: a substance that flows, light that passes through it, motion that runs smoothly, an asset that becomes cash, a market that absorbs orders, funds kept in cash, a consonant that glides, a diet taken as fluid, and a society that will not hold its shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿「流动」展开：会流的物质、透过它的光、平滑的运行、变成现金的资产、能吸收订单的市场、以现金持有的资金、滑入邻音的音、以流质进食的饮食，以及无法保持形状的社会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water sliding down a glass, clear enough to show the coin beneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：水沿玻璃杯滑下，清澈得能看见杯底的硬币。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE AND ITS CLARITY: what flows also lets light through, and both belong to water.
branches.cn: 物质与清澈：会流之物也让光透过，二者都属于水。

branches.en: SMOOTH PASSAGE: motion and consonants alike glide into what follows without a stop.
branches.cn: 平滑过渡：动作与辅音都不阻塞地滑入后接之物。

branches.en: MONEY THAT FLOWS: an asset becomes cash, and the firm keeps its wealth in that form.
branches.cn: 会流的钱：资产变成现金，企业以该形式持有财富。

branches.en: THE MARKET'S DEPTH: many ready buyers let a large order pass without moving the price.
branches.cn: 市场的深度：众多现成买家让大额订单通过而不推动价格。

branches.en: CARE AND METAPHOR: a diet taken as fluid, and a society whose arrangements will not hold their shape.
branches.cn: 照护与隐喻：以流质进食的饮食，以及安排无法定形的社会。

intro.en: Liquid is a Latin adjective for flowing or clear; the same root supplies the noun for liquidity, the verb for melting and the drink called liquor.
intro.cn: liquid 是表示「流动、清澈」的拉丁形容词；同一词根给出表示流动性的名词、表示熔化的动词，以及名为 liquor 的酒。

latinIntro.en: Latin liquere and liquidus stand behind this whole family, from liquid and liquidity to liquefy and liquor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 liquere 与 liquidus 支撑整个词族，从 liquid、liquidity 到 liquefy 与 liquor。

definition_zh: 偿付能力（资产足以覆盖负债、能按期清偿债务的能力）

senses.title: The ability to pay long-term debts
senses.titleCN: 偿还长期债务的能力
senses.definition: the condition of being able to meet debts as they fall due out of one's own resources
senses.definitionCN: 能以自己的资源在债务到期时予以清偿的状态
senses.example: The auditors questioned the firm's solvency after two loss-making years.
senses.exampleCN: 连续两年亏损之后，审计师质疑该企业的偿付能力。
senses.why: the noun comes from a Latin verb meaning to loosen or to pay, so solvency is literally the state of being able to untie what one owes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自拉丁语中「松开、清偿」的动词，因此偿付能力字面上就是「能够解开所欠之债」的状态。

senses.title: The balance-sheet test of assets over liabilities
senses.titleCN: 资产负债表上的资产大于负债
senses.definition: the arithmetic condition in which total assets exceed total liabilities
senses.definitionCN: 总资产超过总负债的算术条件
senses.example: On paper the company passed the solvency test with room to spare.
senses.exampleCN: 账面上，这家公司通过偿付检验，还有余量。
senses.why: once debts are written down as liabilities, being able to pay becomes a comparison of two totals rather than a promise.
senses.whyCN: 债务一旦记为负债，能否清偿就变成两个总额的比较，而不是一句承诺。

senses.title: Regulatory solvency for banks
senses.titleCN: 银行监管意义上的偿付能力
senses.definition: the capital a bank must hold above its risk-weighted assets to absorb losses
senses.definitionCN: 银行必须在风险加权资产之上持有、用于吸收损失的资本
senses.example: The bank was told to raise capital to restore its solvency ratio.
senses.exampleCN: 该行被要求补充资本，以恢复偿付能力比率。
senses.why: a bank's losses can exceed its capital in a single quarter, so a regulator demands a buffer before that happens.
senses.whyCN: 银行一个季度的损失就可能超过资本，监管者因此要求事前留出缓冲。

senses.title: Solvency capital for insurers
senses.titleCN: 保险公司的偿付能力资本
senses.definition: the funds an insurer must keep so that it can pay claims even after a large shock
senses.definitionCN: 保险公司即使遭遇重大冲击后仍能赔付所需的资金
senses.example: The insurer held solvency capital well above the minimum.
senses.exampleCN: 这家保险公司持有的偿付能力资本远高于最低要求。
senses.why: claims arrive after a shock, so an insurer must hold funds that can be paid out even in a bad year.
senses.whyCN: 赔付在冲击之后才到来，保险公司必须持有即使坏年份也能付出的资金。

senses.title: A corporate solvency crisis
senses.titleCN: 企业的偿付能力危机
senses.definition: a situation in which a firm's assets no longer cover its debts and rescue becomes urgent
senses.definitionCN: 企业资产已不足以覆盖债务、亟需救助的局面
senses.example: The solvency crisis began when the pension deficit was counted.
senses.exampleCN: 偿付能力危机在养老金缺口被计入时开始。
senses.why: a pension deficit can turn a profitable firm into one whose assets no longer cover its promises.
senses.whyCN: 养老金缺口能把一家盈利企业变成资产不再覆盖承诺的企业。

senses.title: Sovereign solvency
senses.titleCN: 国家层面的偿付能力
senses.definition: the ability of a state to service its public debt without default
senses.definitionCN: 一国在不违约的情况下偿还公共债务的能力
senses.example: Sovereign solvency depends on growth as much as on the deficit.
senses.exampleCN: 国家的偿付能力既取决于赤字，也同样取决于增长。
senses.why: a state cannot be liquidated, so its solvency is judged by its capacity to tax and grow rather than by a sale.
senses.whyCN: 国家不能被变卖，其偿付能力因此以征税与增长能力而非出售来评判。

senses.title: The solvency ratio as a number
senses.titleCN: 作为数字的偿付能力比率
senses.definition: a measure comparing capital or assets with liabilities or risk exposures
senses.definitionCN: 比较资本或资产与负债或风险敞口的指标
senses.example: A solvency ratio of one means assets exactly equal liabilities.
senses.exampleCN: 偿付能力比率等于一，意味着资产恰好等于负债。
senses.why: a single number lets supervisors compare very different institutions, so the condition is compressed into a ratio.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字能让监管者比较差别很大的机构，状态因此被压成比率。

senses.title: Solvency of a pension fund
senses.titleCN: 养老基金的偿付能力
senses.definition: whether a fund's assets plus expected income can cover the promises it has made
senses.definitionCN: 基金的资产加上预期收入能否覆盖其已作出的承诺
senses.example: The fund's solvency improved as bond yields rose.
senses.exampleCN: 随着债券收益率上升，该基金的偿付能力有所改善。
senses.why: promises extend decades beyond the assets on hand, so the fund must be judged against future payments.
senses.whyCN: 承诺比手头资产延伸得多数十年，基金因此必须对着未来支付来评判。

intro.en: Solvency comes from Latin solvere 'to loosen, to pay' through the present participle solvens and Late Latin solventia. English formed the noun in the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solvency 经拉丁 solvere「松开、清偿」的现在分词 solvens 与晚期拉丁 solventia 而来，英语在 18 世纪构成该名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solvere meant 'to loosen, untie, dissolve, and also to pay'. The paying sense grew from the image of untying a debt, and the deeper origin is usually analysed as a prefix plus a verb for loosening, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、解开、溶解」，也指「清偿」。清偿义从「解开债务」的意象生长出来；更深来源通常分析为前缀加「松开」动词，属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.en: The present participle solvens 'loosening, paying' described a person or estate that could meet its obligations.
items.cn: 现在分词 solvens「正在松开、正在清偿」描述能够履行义务的人或产业。

items.en: Late Latin solventia named the capacity to pay, and the abstract noun passed into French and then English.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 solventia 指清偿能力，这一抽象名词经法语进入英语。

items.en: English solvency is recorded in commercial writing of the early eighteenth century, in contrast with insolvency.
items.cn: 英语 solvency 见于 18 世纪初的商业写作，与无力偿付相对。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries turned the idea into ratios, as banks and insurers were required to hold capital against losses.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪把这一观念变成比率，银行与保险公司被要求持有资本以抵御损失。

items.en: Pension funds, sovereigns and whole financial systems are now tested for solvency, so the word covers every scale of debtor.
items.cn: 养老基金、国家乃至整个金融体系如今都要接受偿付能力检验，这个词因此覆盖各种规模的债务人。

note.en: Group one holds words from the loosening root; group two holds terms that measure a different kind of financial health.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「松开」词根的词；第二组是衡量另一种财务健康的术语。

entries.tag: the adjective; also a chemical noun
entries.definition: Able to pay debts; the same form also names a dissolving liquid, so context decides.
entries.definitionCN: 指有能力偿债；同一形式也指溶解液体，须靠语境分辨。

entries.definition: The inability to pay debts; it is the state that bankruptcy procedures address.
entries.definitionCN: 指无力偿债；正是破产程序所处理的状态。

entries.definition: An answer to a problem, or a liquid mixture; both come from loosening, not from paying.
entries.definitionCN: 指问题的解答或液体混合物；二者都出自「松开」而非「清偿」。

entries.definition: To break a substance into a liquid, or to end an assembly; the paying sense is absent.
entries.definitionCN: 指使物质溶入液体或解散集会；不含清偿义。

entries.definition: Whether cash is available this week; solvency asks whether assets cover debts at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指这周是否有现金可用；偿付能力问资产是否根本覆盖债务。

entries.definition: How safe a borrower looks to a lender; it is a judgement, while solvency is an accounting condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指借款人在放贷者眼中的安全程度；它是判断，而偿付能力是会计条件。

entries.definition: The ratio of capital to risk-weighted assets; it is the banking test of solvency in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指资本与风险加权资产的比率；它是偿付能力在银行实践中的检验。

entries.definition: Failure to pay on time; a single default may be cured, while insolvency is a lasting condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指未能按时付款；单次违约可以补救，而无力偿债是持续状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: To solve and to pay are the same verb in Latin: untying a debt and untying a knot share an image.
normal.cn: 在拉丁语里，「解决」与「清偿」是同一个动词：解开债务与解开绳结共用同一意象。

normal.en: The family runs solve, solution, solvent, solvency, insolvent, insolvency, dissolve.
normal.cn: 同族词包括解决、解法、溶剂、偿付能力、无力偿付的、无力偿付、溶解。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the tests: solvency ratio, solvency risk, solvency capital requirement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出检验：偿付能力比率、偿付能力风险、偿付能力资本要求。

normal.en: Solvency compares totals on a balance sheet; liquidity compares cash with this month's bills.
normal.cn: 偿付能力比较资产负债表上的总额；流动性比较现金与本月的账单。

normal.en: The opposite is not bankruptcy but insolvency: the condition comes first, the procedure later.
normal.cn: 反义不是破产而是无力偿付：状态先出现，程序随后才来。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with assets on one pan and debts on the other, still tipped toward the assets.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一盘资产、一盘债务，仍向资产一端倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a knot being untied slowly, one debt at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个绳结被慢慢解开，一次一笔债务。

abstract.en: Picture a hospital chart where the vital sign is not pulse but the gap between two totals.
abstract.cn: 想象一张病房图表，关键指标不是脉搏，而是两个总额之间的差。

examples.en: Solvency is a question of totals, not of this month's cash.
examples.cn: 偿付能力是总额的问题，而不是本月现金的问题。

examples.en: The regulator closed the bank once its solvency ratio fell below the floor.
examples.cn: 偿付能力比率跌破下限后，监管者关闭了这家银行。

examples.en: Rising rates improved the pension fund's solvency without any new contributions.
examples.cn: 利率上升改善了养老基金的偿付能力，且无需任何新缴款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「解开」的词根加名词后缀——能把欠下的债一个个解开，就是有偿付能力

root: 拉丁 solvere「松开、解开、清偿」= 前缀「分开」+ 表示「松开」的动词，更深来源属重构；其现在分词 solvens 与晚期拉丁 solventia 给出 solvency，18 世纪入英语。同根词有 solve、solution、dissolve、dissolution。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all weigh two totals: what is owned against what is owed. The weighing is done for a firm, a balance sheet, a bank, an insurer, a failing company, a state, a published ratio and a pension fund.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在称量两个总额：拥有的与欠下的。称量对象分别是企业、资产负债表、银行、保险公司、陷入困境的公司、国家、公开的比率与养老基金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with assets on one pan and debts on the other, still tipped toward assets.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平，一盘资产、一盘债务，仍向资产一端倾斜。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY AND THE SUM: being able to pay, and the arithmetic that shows it.
branches.cn: 能力与总和：能够清偿，以及证明这一点的算术。

branches.en: REGULATED CAPITAL: banks and insurers must hold a buffer above expected losses.
branches.cn: 受监管的资本：银行与保险公司必须在预期损失之上持有缓冲。

branches.en: THE FIRM IN TROUBLE: when assets no longer cover debts, rescue becomes urgent.
branches.cn: 陷入困境的企业：资产不再覆盖债务时，救助变得急迫。

branches.en: THE STATE AS DEBTOR: a country's growth and deficit decide whether it can service its debt.
branches.cn: 作为债务人的国家：增长与赤字决定它能否偿还债务。

branches.en: NUMBERS AND PROMISES: a ratio is published, and a fund is tested against promises made long ago.
branches.cn: 数字与承诺：比率被公布，基金则要对着多年前作出的承诺受检。

intro.en: Solvency is an abstract noun built on a Latin verb for loosening, which also supplies the words for solving and dissolving.
intro.cn: solvency 是建立在拉丁语「松开」动词上的抽象名词，同一动词还给出「解决」与「溶解」等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere and its participle solvens stand behind solve, solution, solvent, solvency and dissolve.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 solvere 及其分词 solvens 支撑 solve、solution、solvent、solvency 与 dissolve。

items.example: The verb joins a knot and a debt.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时连接绳结与债务。

items.meaning: an untying; an answer; a liquid mixture

items.exampleCN: 这家企业仍有偿付能力。

items.meaning: the state of being unable to pay

items.example: The dissolution of the partnership took a year.
items.exampleCN: 合伙关系的解散花了一年。

definition_zh: 有偿付能力的；有溶解力的；溶剂（能溶解其他物质的液体）
definition_en: able to pay one's debts, or having the power to dissolve something; a substance that dissolves another
core_image: 一只玻璃瓶里透明液体正把糖块化开，瓶身贴着一张「已结清」的标签
scene: 检验员把一块树脂放进溶剂，几分钟后它完全化开。The inspector dropped a piece of resin into the solvent and watched it dissolve within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里指「能溶解其他物质的液体」（第 2 个义项：作为溶剂的物质）；句意为检验员把一块树脂放进溶剂，几分钟后它完全化开。可辨识物件：玻璃瓶、糖块、结清标签、量勺。

pos.zh: 有偿付能力的；有溶解力的
溶剂；溶解介质

否定前缀加基础形容词 → 无力偿付的
