senses.title: Financially able to pay debts
senses.titleCN: 财务上有能力清偿债务
senses.definition: describing a person or firm whose assets exceed liabilities and which can meet its obligations
senses.definitionCN: 描述资产超过负债、能够履行义务的个人或企业
senses.example: The company stayed solvent through the downturn by selling a division.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司靠出售一个部门在低迷期保持偿付能力。
senses.why: the adjective is the present participle of the Latin verb for loosening: one who can untie a debt is solvent.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词是拉丁语「松开」动词的现在分词：能解开债务的人就是有偿付能力的。

senses.title: A liquid that dissolves another substance
senses.titleCN: 能把另一种物质溶开的液体
senses.definition: in chemistry, the component of a mixture that does the dissolving, usually the larger part
senses.definitionCN: 化学中混合物里执行溶解的那个组分，通常占较大部分
senses.example: Water is the solvent in most biological reactions.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数生物反应中，水是溶剂。
senses.why: in a mixture one component must do the dissolving, and the larger, more mobile part is usually it.
senses.whyCN: 混合物中必须有一个组分执行溶解，通常就是占得更多、更易移动的那一部分。

senses.title: Having the power to dissolve
senses.titleCN: 具有溶解能力的
senses.definition: describing a substance or agent that can break another material into a solution
senses.definitionCN: 描述能把另一种材料化为溶液的物质或作用者
senses.example: The solvent power of the new cleaner surprised the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 这种新清洁剂的溶解力让实验室感到意外。
senses.why: the same participle can describe the agent instead of the mixture, which is why the word works as an adjective in chemistry too.
senses.whyCN: 同一分词也能描述起作用者而非混合物，因此这个词在化学里也作形容词。

senses.title: An industrial or household cleaning liquid
senses.titleCN: 工业或家用清洁液体
senses.definition: a volatile liquid used to remove grease, paint or resin in workshops and homes
senses.definitionCN: 在车间与家中用于去除油污、油漆或树脂的挥发性液体
senses.example: The workshop banned the old solvent after the ventilation report.
senses.exampleCN: 通风报告之后，车间禁用了那种旧溶剂。
senses.why: grease and resin will not wash away in water, so workshops need a stronger liquid to carry them off.
senses.whyCN: 油脂与树脂不能靠水洗掉，车间因此需要更强的液体把它们带走。

senses.title: Solvent abuse as inhalants
senses.titleCN: 作为吸入剂的溶剂滥用
senses.definition: the practice of inhaling fumes from glues and cleaners for a short-lived high
senses.definitionCN: 为获得短暂快感而吸入胶水或清洁剂蒸气的行为
senses.example: Solvent abuse among teenagers worried the school.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年吸食溶剂让学校担忧。
senses.why: the same volatile fumes that dissolve grease can be inhaled, which is why the word appears in warnings.
senses.whyCN: 溶开油脂的同一挥发性蒸气也能被吸入，因此这个词出现在警示语中。

senses.title: A solvent estate in law
senses.titleCN: 法律上足以清偿的遗产
senses.definition: an estate whose assets are enough to pay the deceased person's debts and gifts
senses.definitionCN: 资产足以支付死者债务与遗赠的遗产
senses.example: The executor confirmed that the estate was solvent.
senses.exampleCN: 遗嘱执行人确认这笔遗产足以清偿。
senses.why: the test for an estate is the same as for a firm: do the assets cover what must be paid out?
senses.whyCN: 对遗产的检验与对企业相同：资产是否覆盖必须付出的款项？

senses.title: Solvent extraction as a process
senses.titleCN: 作为工艺的溶剂萃取
senses.definition: a method that uses a liquid to pull a wanted substance out of a solid or another liquid
senses.definitionCN: 用液体把目标物质从固体或另一液体中提取出来的方法
senses.example: Oil is often recovered by solvent extraction from crushed seed.
senses.exampleCN: 油常通过溶剂萃取从压碎的种子中提取。
senses.why: a liquid can carry a wanted substance out of a solid, which turns the chemical property into an industrial method.
senses.whyCN: 液体能把目标物质从固体中带出，这一化学性质于是变成工业方法。

senses.title: Solvent-free products
senses.titleCN: 不含溶剂的产品
senses.definition: describing paints, glues or cleaners made without volatile organic liquids
senses.definitionCN: 描述不使用挥发性有机液体的油漆、胶水或清洁剂
senses.example: The builder switched to solvent-free adhesives for indoor work.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方在室内作业改用无溶剂胶黏剂。
senses.why: if the fumes are the problem, the simplest fix is to make the product without any solvent at all.
senses.whyCN: 如果问题出在蒸气，最简单的办法就是完全不用溶剂来制造产品。

intro.en: Solvent is the present participle of Latin solvere 'to loosen, pay'. English uses it for both paying and dissolving because the Latin verb covers both. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solvent 是拉丁 solvere「松开、清偿」的现在分词。英语用它兼指偿付与溶解，因为拉丁动词本来就覆盖两义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solvere meant 'to loosen, untie, dissolve, pay'. The two modern senses of solvent were both present in the Latin verb, one as untying a debt and one as loosening a substance.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、解开、溶解、清偿」。solvent 的两个现代义在拉丁动词中都已存在，一是解开债务，一是溶开物质。

items.en: The present participle solvens meant 'loosening, paying', and English took the form directly rather than through a noun.
items.cn: 现在分词 solvens 意为「正在松开、正在清偿」，英语直接吸收这一形式，而非经由名词。

items.en: Alchemists and later chemists used solvent for the liquid that dissolves a solid, a sense recorded in English from the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 炼金术士与后来的化学家用 solvent 指溶解固体的液体，这一义自 17 世纪见于英语。

items.en: The financial sense, able to pay what one owes, is also recorded in the seventeenth century and rests on the paying half of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 「能够清偿所欠」的财务义同样见于 17 世纪，依据的是拉丁动词中「清偿」的那一半。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries made solvents ordinary industrial materials, and the word spread to cleaning, painting and extraction.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪使溶剂成为寻常工业材料，这个词扩展到清洁、涂装与萃取。

items.en: Late in the twentieth century, concern about fumes produced the compound solvent-free and a new sense of the word.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期对蒸气的担忧产生了「无溶剂」这一复合词与该词的新义。

note.en: Group one holds words from the loosening root or the same chemical field; group two holds financial adjectives that are often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「松开」词根或同属化学领域的词；第二组是常与它混淆的财务形容词。

entries.tag: the dissolved thing, not the liquid
entries.definition: The substance that is dissolved; the solvent is what does the dissolving, so the two are opposites in a mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 指被溶解的物质；溶剂是执行溶解的一方，二者在混合物中相对。

entries.definition: The resulting mixture of solute and solvent, or an answer to a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 指溶质与溶剂形成的混合物，或问题的解答。

entries.definition: Describing the solute that can go into a solvent; it does not describe the liquid itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能进入溶剂的溶质；并不描述液体本身。

entries.tag: the noun of the financial sense
entries.definition: The ability to pay debts; the adjective for that ability is solvent.
entries.definitionCN: 指偿债能力；表示该能力的形容词正是 solvent。

entries.definition: Judged safe to lend to; a firm can be solvent yet judged uncreditworthy.
entries.definitionCN: 指被认为可以安全放贷；企业可以有偿付能力却仍被认为不宜放贷。

entries.definition: Able to turn assets into cash quickly; solvency concerns totals, not speed.
entries.definitionCN: 指能迅速把资产变成现金；偿付能力关乎总额，而非速度。

entries.tag: a rare synonym for the chemical noun
entries.definition: A dissolving agent, used in technical writing; solvent is the common form.
entries.definitionCN: 指起溶解作用之物，用于技术写作；solvent 是常见形式。

entries.definition: Describing an amount that must be paid; solvent describes the one who can pay it.
entries.definitionCN: 描述应支付的款项；solvent 描述有能力支付的人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One Latin verb, two jobs: untie a debt and loosen a solid, so solvent means both able to pay and able to dissolve.
normal.cn: 一个拉丁动词干两件事：解开债务与溶开固体，所以这个词既指能清偿，也指能溶解。

normal.en: The family runs solve, solution, soluble, solvent, solvency, insolvent, dissolve.
normal.cn: 同族词包括解决、溶液、可溶的、溶剂、偿付能力、无力偿付的、溶解。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the uses: organic solvent, solvent extraction, solvent abuse, remain solvent.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出用法：有机溶剂、溶剂萃取、吸食溶剂、保持偿付能力。

normal.en: In a mixture the solvent is the liquid, the solute is what disappears into it.
normal.cn: 在混合物中，溶剂是液体，溶质是溶进其中的东西。

normal.en: Solvent-free paint is a modern label made by putting the old word in front of free.
normal.cn: 无溶剂油漆是把旧词放在「无」前面造出的现代标签。

abstract.en: Picture a clear liquid eating a sugar lump while a settled bill hangs on the bottle.
abstract.cn: 想象一瓶透明液体正在化开糖块，瓶上挂着已结清的账单。

abstract.en: Picture a knot coming undone with no knife, only patience.
abstract.cn: 想象一个绳结在没有刀的情况下慢慢解开，只靠耐心。

abstract.en: Picture two faces of one coin: one reads able to pay, the other reads able to dissolve.
abstract.cn: 想象同一枚硬币的两面：一面写「能清偿」，一面写「能溶解」。

examples.en: The firm remained solvent even after the loss, because its property was worth more than its debt.
examples.cn: 即使出现亏损，这家企业仍有偿付能力，因为其房产价值高于债务。

examples.en: Use the solvent outdoors; the fumes are heavier than air.
examples.cn: 要在户外使用这种溶剂，其蒸气比空气重。

examples.en: The estate was solvent, so every creditor was paid in full.
examples.cn: 这笔遗产足以清偿，因此每位债权人都获得全额支付。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「解开」的词根加表示「……的」的后缀——能解开债务的是有偿付能力的，能解开物质的则成了溶剂

root: 拉丁 solvere「松开、解开、溶解、清偿」的现在分词 solvens 直接进入英语；同一动词的过去分词与名词形式给出 solution、solvency，同根还有 dissolve、absolve。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses use one participle in two fields: a payer who can untie debts, and a liquid that unties solids, then the cleaning trade, inhalant misuse, estates, extraction and products made without it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个分词用在两个领域：能解开债务的清偿者，能溶开固体的液体，随后是清洁行业、吸入滥用、遗产、萃取，以及不含它的产品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear liquid eating a sugar lump, with a settled bill hanging on the bottle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一瓶透明液体正在化开糖块，瓶上挂着已结清的账单。

branches.en: THE PAYER: a person, a firm or an estate that can untie what it owes.
branches.cn: 清偿者：能解开所欠之债的个人、企业或遗产。

branches.en: THE LIQUID AND ITS POWER: the dissolving component, and the strength it brings.
branches.cn: 液体与力量：执行溶解的组分，以及它所带的溶解力。

branches.en: THE TRADE: cleaning fluids and extraction methods turn the chemical sense into work.
branches.cn: 行业：清洁液与萃取方法把化学义变成工作。

branches.en: MISUSE: the same fumes that clean metal can be inhaled.
branches.cn: 滥用：清洁金属的同一蒸气也可被吸入。

branches.en: THE NEGATIVE FORM: modern products are labelled by the absence of the solvent.
branches.cn: 否定形式：现代产品以「不含溶剂」来标注。

intro.en: Solvent is one Latin participle serving two English fields; the root also gives solve, solution, soluble and dissolve.
intro.cn: solvent 是一个拉丁分词，服务于两个英语领域；同一词根还给出 solve、solution、soluble 与 dissolve。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere and solvens stand behind the whole family, from solution to insolvency.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 solvere 与 solvens 支撑整个词族，从 solution 到 insolvency。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词覆盖两个领域。

items.example: The participle became an English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词变成了英语词。

items.example: They solved the shortage by importing.
items.exampleCN: 他们靠进口解决了短缺。

items.example: The court absolved him of blame.

definition_zh: 破产（无力清偿债务的法律状态或司法程序）
definition_en: the legal state or procedure of being unable to pay one's debts
core_image: 一张被砸断的长凳，木片散落在钱币兑换商的门前
scene: 订单断了三个月后，这家工厂向法院申请破产，债权人开始登记申报。After three months without orders, the factory filed for bankruptcy, and its creditors began to register their claims.
sceneCN: 这里指「因无力偿债而进入的法律程序」（第 1 个义项：经法院处理的破产状态）；句意为断单三个月后，这家工厂向法院申请破产，债权人开始登记申报。可辨识物件：断凳、法院门牌、债权登记表、封条。

pos.zh: 破产（可数或不可数；复数 bankruptcies）

derivatives.zh: 长凳词根加「断」的分词词根 → 破产的；使破产；破产者
短语意象中的基础名词，义为「长凳、钱桌」→ 银行
否定前缀加「偿付能力」名词 → 无力偿付
基础形容词加动词后缀 → 清算
「断」的词根加名词后缀 → 断裂；破裂

senses.title: The legal status of being unable to pay
senses.titleCN: 无力清偿债务的法律状态
senses.definition: the formal condition, recognised by a court, in which a debtor cannot meet its debts
senses.definitionCN: 经法院认定、债务人无法履行债务的正式状态
senses.example: The court placed the firm in bankruptcy after the payment deadline passed.
senses.exampleCN: 付款期限过后，法院使这家企业进入破产状态。
senses.why: the word began as a broken bench, so the legal status keeps the image of a trader put out of business.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指被砸断的长凳，法律状态因此保留商人被逐出营业的意象。

senses.title: Liquidation of the debtor's assets
senses.titleCN: 变卖债务人资产以清偿
senses.definition: the procedure in which assets are sold and the proceeds divided among creditors
senses.definitionCN: 变卖资产并把所得分给债权人的程序
senses.example: Bankruptcy ended with the mill sold and the workers paid first.
senses.exampleCN: 破产以工厂被出售、工人先获清偿而结束。
senses.why: if the business cannot continue, the assets must be turned into money so creditors can be paid in order.
senses.whyCN: 企业若无法继续，资产必须换成钱，债权人才能按顺序获偿。

senses.title: Reorganisation instead of sale
senses.titleCN: 以重整代替变卖
senses.definition: a procedure that keeps the business running while debts are restructured
senses.definitionCN: 在重组债务的同时让企业继续运营的程序
senses.example: The airline used bankruptcy to renegotiate its leases, not to close.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司借破产重新谈租约，而非关门。
senses.why: a business may be worth more alive than sold, so the law offers a route that keeps it running while debts are rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 企业活着可能比卖掉更值钱，法律因此提供一条让它继续运营、同时重组债务的路径。

senses.title: Personal bankruptcy
senses.titleCN: 个人破产
senses.definition: the same legal route taken by an individual rather than a company
senses.definitionCN: 由个人而非企业走上的同一法律路径
senses.example: Personal bankruptcy cleared the medical debts but ruined her credit.
senses.exampleCN: 个人破产免除了医疗债务，却毁了她的信用。
senses.why: a person can owe more than he owns just as a company can, so the same procedure is offered to individuals.
senses.whyCN: 个人也会像企业一样欠得比拥有的多，同一程序因此也向个人开放。

senses.title: The figurative collapse of an idea or system
senses.titleCN: 观念或体系的比喻性崩解
senses.definition: a total failure of a scheme, theory or institution, without any court involved
senses.definitionCN: 计划、理论或机构的彻底失败，与法院无关
senses.example: The report described the plan as a moral and economic bankruptcy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称该计划在道义与经济上均已破产。
senses.why: the broken bench can be imagined anywhere, so any total failure is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 断凳可以被想象在任何地方，任何彻底的失败便都用同一个词描述。

senses.title: Moral bankruptcy in public life
senses.titleCN: 公共生活中的道德破产
senses.definition: the loss of credibility or ethical standing of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体失去公信力或道德地位
senses.example: The scandal exposed the moral bankruptcy of the leadership.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻暴露出领导层的道德破产。
senses.why: when credibility rather than money is gone, the word still fits, because nothing is left to pay with.
senses.whyCN: 当失去的是公信力而非金钱时，这个词仍然合用，因为已无东西可付。

senses.title: The act of filing a petition
senses.titleCN: 提交破产申请的动作
senses.definition: the formal step by which a debtor or creditor starts the procedure
senses.definitionCN: 债务人或债权人启动程序的形式步骤
senses.example: The filing for bankruptcy came on a Friday afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 破产申请是在一个周五下午提交的。
senses.why: the procedure begins with a document, so the act of filing is spoken of as the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 程序从一份文书开始，因此提交的动作本身被当作事件来说。

senses.title: Bankruptcy protection and the automatic stay
senses.titleCN: 破产保护与自动中止
senses.definition: the court order that pauses collection and lawsuits while the case proceeds
senses.definitionCN: 案件进行期间暂停追债与诉讼的法院命令
senses.example: Bankruptcy protection stopped the bank from seizing the equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 破产保护阻止了银行扣押设备。
senses.why: creditors would otherwise race to seize assets, so a court order freezes collection while the case is sorted out.
senses.whyCN: 否则债权人会抢先扣押资产，法院命令因此在案件理清期间冻结追债。

senses.title: Fraudulent bankruptcy
senses.titleCN: 欺诈性破产
senses.definition: the offence of hiding or transferring assets before or during insolvency
senses.definitionCN: 在无力偿付之前或期间藏匿、转移资产的罪行
senses.example: Two directors were charged with fraudulent bankruptcy.
senses.exampleCN: 两名董事被控欺诈性破产。
senses.why: hiding assets before the case defeats the purpose of the law, so the conduct is made a separate offence.
senses.whyCN: 在案发前藏匿资产会摧毁法律的目的，因此该行为被单列为罪行。

intro.en: Bankruptcy comes from Italian banca rotta 'broken bench', the table of a money changer who could not pay. The image reached English through French and Latin forms in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bankruptcy 来自意大利语 banca rotta「被砸断的长凳」，即无力清偿的钱币兑换商的桌子。这一意象于 16 世纪经法语与拉丁形式进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: A banca was the bench or table where a money changer and his coins sat in a public square.
items.cn: banca 指钱币兑换商与他的钱币在公共广场上占据的长凳或桌子。

items.en: Rumpere meant 'to break', and its participle ruptus supplied the second half of banca rotta.
items.cn: rumpere 意为「打断」，其分词 ruptus 提供 banca rotta 的后一半。

items.en: In Italian practice a trader who could not pay might have his bench broken, a public sign that he could no longer do business.
items.cn: 在意大利的惯例中，无力清偿的商人可能被砸断长凳，公开表明他不能再做生意。

items.en: French borrowed the image as banqueroute, and English took the noun in the sixteenth century in forms such as bankrupt.
items.cn: 法语把这个意象借为 banqueroute，英语于 16 世纪以 bankrupt 一类形式吸收该名词。

items.en: The abstract noun bankruptcy was formed in English on the model of French, adding the ending that names a state or procedure.
items.cn: 抽象名词 bankruptcy 在英语中仿法语构成，加上表示状态或程序的词尾。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries turned the image into a statute-based procedure with liquidation, reorganisation, protection and criminal forms.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪把这一意象变成以成文法为基础的程序，包含清算、重整、保护与犯罪形态。

note.en: Group one holds words from the broken-bench image or from breaking; group two holds legal and financial terms that are often used as if they were synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是出自「断凳」意象或「打断」词根的词；第二组是常被当作同义词使用的法律与金融术语。

entries.definition: A debtor legally declared unable to pay, or the act of making someone so; bankruptcy is the state or case.
entries.definitionCN: 指被依法宣告无力清偿的债务人，或使某人如此的行为；bankruptcy 指状态或案件。

entries.definition: The institution that grew from the money changer's bench; the shared origin is invisible in modern use.
entries.definitionCN: 指由钱币商长凳发展而来的机构；共同的来源在现代用法中已看不出来。

entries.definition: A break or burst, often of a pipe or a relationship; it has nothing to do with money.
entries.definitionCN: 指断裂或爆裂，常用于管道或关系；与金钱无关。

entries.definition: To break into something in progress; the prefix means between, and no debt is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 指打断进行中的事情；前缀意为「在……之间」，不涉债务。

entries.definition: The accounting state of owing more than one owns; bankruptcy is the legal procedure that may follow.
entries.definitionCN: 指欠得比拥有的多的会计状态；bankruptcy 是随后可能启动的法律程序。

entries.definition: The selling off of assets; it is one form bankruptcy can take, not the whole procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 指变卖资产；它是破产可能采取的一种形式，而非整个程序。

entries.definition: Failure to pay on a due date; a default can occur without any bankruptcy case being opened.
entries.definitionCN: 指到期未付；违约可以在未启动任何破产案件时发生。

entries.definition: Control of a company given to an outside officer for creditors; it is a separate legal route.
entries.definitionCN: 指把公司控制权交给外部官员以维护债权人；是另一条法律路径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The picture is a broken bench: a money changer's table smashed so he cannot trade.
normal.cn: 图景是一张断凳：钱币兑换商的桌子被砸，无法再做买卖。

normal.en: The family runs bankrupt, bankruptcy, bank, rupture, interrupt, disrupt.
normal.cn: 同族词包括破产的、破产、银行、断裂、打断、扰乱。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the steps: file for, declare, protection, proceedings.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出步骤：申请、宣布、保护、程序。

normal.en: The bench survives in bank, and the breaking survives in rupture.
normal.cn: 那张长凳留在银行一词里，打断的动作留在断裂一词里。

normal.en: A filing is not a closure: protection can keep the business alive while debts are rebuilt.
normal.cn: 申请并不等于关门：保护可以让企业在债务重组期间继续运营。

abstract.en: Picture splinters of a wooden bench on the stones of a market square.
abstract.cn: 想象木凳的碎片散落在集市广场的石板上。

abstract.en: Picture a shop with the shutters down but the lights still on inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店拉下卷帘，里面的灯却还亮着。

abstract.en: Picture a promise collapsing under its own weight, with no court in sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个承诺在自身重量下崩塌，四周并无法院。

examples.en: The chain filed for bankruptcy after the rent review doubled its costs.
examples.cn: 租金复核使成本翻倍后，这家连锁店申请破产。

examples.en: Bankruptcy protection gave the airline time to renegotiate its leases.
examples.cn: 破产保护给了这家航空公司重新谈租约的时间。

examples.en: Analysts spoke of the bankruptcy of the theory, not of any company.
examples.cn: 分析师说的是这一理论的破产，而非任何公司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「长凳」与「断」两个词根加名词后缀——钱币商的长凳被砸断，做不成买卖 → 破产

root: 意大利语 banca rotta「断凳」：banca「长凳、钱桌」加 rotta，后者出自拉丁 ruptus／rumpere「打断」。经法语 banqueroute 于 16 世纪进入英语，抽象名词仿法语构成。同根词有 rupture、interrupt、disrupt、corrupt、abrupt。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one case: the legal status, the sale of assets, the attempt to keep trading, the individual route, the collapse of an idea, moral collapse, the filing itself, the protection that pauses creditors, and the criminal form.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个案件展开：法律状态、变卖资产、设法继续经营、个人路径、观念的崩解、道德崩解、申请的动作、暂停追债的保护，以及犯罪形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smashed bench on the stones of a market square.
core.cn: 核心意象：集市广场石板上的一张被砸断的长凳。

branches.en: STATUS AND PETITION: the condition is declared, and someone must file to start it.
branches.cn: 状态与申请：条件被宣告，且必须有人提交申请才能启动。

branches.en: TWO OUTCOMES: the assets are sold, or the business is kept alive and the debts rebuilt.
branches.cn: 两种结局：资产被变卖，或企业继续存活、债务被重组。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL: a person can take the same route as a company.
branches.cn: 个人：一个人可以走与企业相同的路径。

branches.en: THE WORD WITHOUT A COURT: an idea or a leadership can be called bankrupt in plain speech.
branches.cn: 无需法院的词：观念或领导层可以在日常语言中被称为破产。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND ABUSE: the law pauses collection, and the law also punishes hidden assets.
branches.cn: 保护与滥用：法律暂停追债，法律也惩罚藏匿资产。

intro.en: Bankruptcy joins the bench of the money changer with a Latin participle for broken; the breaking root also builds rupture, interrupt and corrupt.
intro.cn: bankruptcy 把钱币兑换商的长凳与表示「被打断」的拉丁分词连在一起；这一词根还构成 rupture、interrupt 与 corrupt。

latinIntro.en: Latin rumpere 'to break' and its participle ruptus supply the second half of the word; banca is Italian for the bench.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rumpere「打断」及其分词 ruptus 提供该词的后一半；banca 是意大利语中的长凳。

items.meaning: the state of a broken bench

items.example: The meeting came to an abrupt end.
